original_source: Planned network maintenance on May 24, 2011, to resolve router performance and multicast issues.
failure_pattern: During the scheduled maintenance, the reboots of the Foundry routers and switches ran out of the allotted window, causing incomplete upgrades and abrupt network changes. The abrupt reboots triggered a crash in the NIC driver on several database servers, which removed them from the cluster and led to intermittent site downtime and degraded page load performance.
mitigation_principle: allocate sufficient maintenance window; perform comprehensive pre‑maintenance testing; implement graceful reboot procedures; validate NIC driver compatibility; establish rollback plan; monitor database cluster health during maintenance

original_source: Performance and access issues across WMF web properties due to database load and LoadMonitor behavior on 23rd June 2011.
symptoms: back‑end request failures causing squid errors
failure_pattern: The LoadMonitor software generated an excessive number of connections to the S7/CentralAuth databases, exhausting the maximum thread pool and causing database errors. These errors cascaded to back‑end services, leading to failed requests and widespread access and performance problems across the web properties.
mitigation_principle: implement robust load monitoring and alerting; disable or limit max threads to prevent exhaustion; capture and display meaningful error messages; maintain redundant contact lists for escalation; document failure modes and conduct post‑mortem reviews; measure database load without establishing connections

original_source: Service interruption during planned network maintenance on July 13, 2011, due to NIC driver issues after switch reload
failure_pattern: During the planned maintenance, a switch reload caused brief network connectivity loss on database servers. The NIC driver (forcedeth) failed to recover automatically, requiring manual reset of network software on each server, which resulted in a rolling service interruption lasting about 25 minutes.
mitigation_principle: implement graceful switch reload procedures; test NIC driver resilience before maintenance; add network connectivity monitoring; use redundant NICs; apply driver updates; perform pre-maintenance connectivity checks; enable automated failover

original_source: Access switch power outage, database master switch issues, and replication hang due to long-running queries in Tampa data center.
symptoms: high load due to cache loss
failure_pattern: During maintenance, a power cable for the production access switch became loose, causing the switch to power down and disconnect the rack of application servers. The loss of network connectivity triggered Nagios alerts and overloaded services, while the subsequent database master switch operation introduced long-running queries that stalled replication, leading to a site-wide outage.
mitigation_principle: Separate and label power cables for access and management switches; retrofit older racks with redundant power and uplinks; add memcached redundancy; suppress slave lag checks during read-only mode; isolate CentralAuth to dedicated cluster; prevent flush tables replication during master switch; terminate long-running queries before master switch

original_source: Access switch power outage in Tampa data center due to accidental disconnection during management switch replacement
symptoms: slow page loads due to cache miss
failure_pattern: During a management switch replacement, an access switch was accidentally disconnected from power, causing the switch to lose power for about 18 minutes. This outage took down the rack of application servers connected to that switch, resulting in loss of memcached caching and forcing MediaWiki to regenerate pages, which increased load on the remaining servers.
mitigation_principle: Implement redundant power and uplinks for access switches; retrofit older racks with redundant power; enforce strict disconnect procedures during maintenance; use redundant network paths

original_source: Database master switchover caused outage due to long-running queries on slave blocking flush tables operation.
symptoms: application errors due to DB unavailability
failure_pattern: During a master switchover, the switch scripts executed a 'flush tables' command on the old master, which replicated to the slaves. The slaves had long-running queries that had created large temporary tables, so the flush tables operation locked all tables and waited for the temp tables to finish, causing the slaves to become unresponsive. This prevented the master switch from completing, resulting in a 10‑minute database outage.
mitigation_principle: prevent replication of flush tables during switchover; automatically kill long-running queries on slaves before switchover; perform pre-switchover health checks to detect long-running queries; avoid flush tables on master during switchover

original_source: Database master switchover for S7 cluster caused 9-minute outage due to overload from CentralAuth slave lag queries
failure_pattern: During a master switchover, the new master was not exempt from CentralAuth queries because the read‑only check was disabled only for MediaWiki. The influx of these queries overloaded the master, blocking normal queries and replication traffic, which caused the sites to become unavailable for about nine minutes.
mitigation_principle: Ensure read‑only checks disable all query types; isolate CentralAuth onto dedicated cluster; implement query throttling during switchover; monitor query load and replication health; add automated fail‑over safeguards to block queries when master is in read‑only mode

original_source: Outage caused by cache stampede on fundraising statistics page after Reddit traffic surge
root_cause_category: cache stampede leading to database overload
failure_pattern: A surge of traffic from Reddit triggered many requests to the fundraising statistics page, whose 15‑minute cache had expired. The heavy database query executed for each request caused a cache stampede, overwhelming the MySQL slave db1025 and later storage3, which in turn produced socket timeouts on Apache servers and made the site unstable.
mitigation_principle: implement cache locking or request coalescing to prevent stampedes; add rate limiting and circuit breakers; increase cache TTL and monitor hit rates; optimize heavy queries; use read replicas and load balancing; add fallback content for cache misses

original_source: Slow page rendering and broken wiki pages due to EQIAD bits server overload from bonding configuration change
symptoms: broken wiki pages due to missing javascript and css
failure_pattern: A change to the interface bonding configuration on the EQIAD bits.wikimedia.org servers caused a loss of connectivity. The resulting packet loss triggered Varnish to spawn excessive threads, overwhelming the servers and leading to slow page rendering and broken pages for users.
mitigation_principle: implement automatic failover for bonded interfaces; enforce limits on Varnish thread creation; monitor network connectivity and cache health; test configuration changes in staging before production; use health checks to detect and recover from interface failures

original_source: Outage caused by human error during squid configuration deploy leading to cache consistency checks and database overload
failure_pattern: An erroneous squid configuration was pushed to upload.wikimedia.org, causing the squids to exit. The deploy process only sent a HUP, so the affected squids failed to reload; the operator then restarted both text and upload squids, triggering forced cache consistency checks that routed all requests to the backend. The resulting flood overwhelmed the database cache, causing many page loads to fail and thumbnails to become unavailable.
mitigation_principle: Deploy configuration changes to a single host and test before cluster rollout; avoid restarting squids to prevent long cache verification; use explicit host lists rather than ranges; test with curl to verify configuration; use deploy tools to enforce host-specific deployments

original_source: Failed static resources on bits.wikimedia.org due to disk space exhaustion and symlink misconfiguration during MediaWiki deployment
component: Apache web server serving static resources
failure_pattern: During a MediaWiki deployment, misconfigured symlinks and insufficient disk space on the static content servers prevented new files from being written and caused existing resources to be inaccessible. The resulting 404 errors manifested as missing images, scripts, and other static assets on bits.wikimedia.org until the disk space issue was resolved and symlinks corrected.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated checks for resource availability during deployments; include symlink validation in deployment scripts; partition storage to avoid artificial resource limits; monitor disk usage proactively; deprecate problematic symlink usage

original_source: API service flapping due to LastModified extension causing excessive POST requests
symptoms: CPU usage maxed out on backend squid
failure_pattern: The LastModified extension caused every page view to issue a POST request to Wikipedia's API, flooding the backend squid with thousands of connections. The squid CPU saturated at 100%, leading to 503 errors and API flapping across the service.
mitigation_principle: Disable or patch problematic extensions; implement request rate limiting; monitor backend CPU and connection counts; ensure monitoring tools are operational; test extensions in staging before deployment

original_source: Intermittent performance problem due to load spike on srv268 affecting memcached and Apache responses.
failure_pattern: A bug in the memcache client caused timeouts to be ignored, which led to an unexpected load spike on srv268. The sudden increase in traffic overwhelmed the memcached and Apache services, resulting in intermittent high latency and slow responses for users.
mitigation_principle: implement robust timeout handling in memcache client; add load monitoring and alerts; use circuit breakers to prevent cascading failures; add redundancy and auto-scaling for memcached and Apache; perform regular load testing and capacity planning

original_source: Wikimedia sites outage on 6th August 2012 due to fiber cut affecting network connectivity between Ashburn and Tampa data centers.
failure_pattern: A third‑party crew severed a fiber optic cable that ran through a folded segment shared by both redundant links between the Ashburn and Tampa data centers, eliminating all network connectivity for backend services and causing the Wikimedia sites to become unavailable.
mitigation_principle: Implement dual independent fiber paths with physical separation; audit fiber routes for single points of failure; use carrier‑provided redundant DWDM systems with diverse routing; perform regular fiber health checks; establish clear coordination with third‑party maintenance crews

original_source: Intermittent performance lags and outages on Wikimedia sites due to Apache load spikes and template-related memory issues in August and September 2012.
root_cause_category: memory exhaustion from template processing and job queue duplication
failure_pattern: Load spikes on Apache triggered intensive page swapping; excessive memory usage from template DOM caching and duplicated job queue caused memory exhaustion, leading to Apache process crashes and reboots, which manifested as intermittent performance lags and brief outages for users.
mitigation_principle: Implement job deduplication and queue size limits; enforce memory usage caps and preprocessor complexity limits; reduce MaxRequestsPerChild; monitor memory and swap usage; add caching and garbage collection; apply rate limiting; perform load testing; enable automated alerts

original_source: TranslationNotifications extension bug triggered by MediaWiki job system changes causing duplicate email notifications
root_cause_category: incorrect job constructor signature causing duplicate job execution
failure_pattern: A bug in the TranslationNotifications extension used an outdated constructor signature. When MediaWiki’s job queue system was updated to enforce stricter constructor requirements and enable job retrying, the extension’s jobs were not properly constructed, causing the queue to treat each retry as a new job and send duplicate email notifications. The lack of documentation and test coverage meant the issue was not detected until it caused widespread duplicate alerts.
mitigation_principle: Improve core system documentation; enforce constructor signature validation; add unit tests for job queue integration; enable job retrying in local test environments; perform code reviews for extension compatibility with core changes; implement automated regression tests for email notifications; audit extensions for similar bugs; provide developer training on core APIs

original_source: Wikimedia sites outage on 15th March 2013 due to database contention from AFTv5 deployment.
symptoms: service degraded for non-edge cached requests
root_cause_category: database contention due to unindexed queries
failure_pattern: The new AFTv5 extension introduced a dedicated database shard that ran unindexed queries with ORDER BY and LIMIT clauses, causing heavy contention on the slave and tying up Apache workers. This prevented edit operations while read traffic continued, resulting in a brief outage for edits.
mitigation_principle: Implement comprehensive indexing and query optimization before deployment; perform load and performance testing on new database shards; monitor database query performance and worker thread usage; use phased rollouts and rollback procedures; enforce database sharding best practices

original_source: Jenkins downtime due to misconfigured Zuul daemon causing inefficient git cloning without hardlinks
symptoms: Jenkins jobs taking excessively long to start
failure_pattern: A misconfigured Zuul daemon caused its git repositories to be cloned from a slow disk to an SSD, forcing git to perform full copies instead of hardlinks. The resulting slow clone operations overwhelmed Jenkins, leading to a massive job queue backlog and eventual service stall.
mitigation_principle: Apply configuration changes consistently across all dependent services; test configuration changes in a staging environment before production; use hardlink-compatible storage for git repositories; monitor disk I/O and clone times; coordinate workspace changes with CI job configurations

original_source: Parsoid LVS services showed as down in Icinga due to expected deployment downtime and monitoring misconfiguration.
symptoms: Parsoid LVS reported as down in Icinga
monitoring alerts continued after service restored
failure_pattern: A planned deployment of Parsoid code and configuration caused a brief service outage; because monitoring was not silenced, Icinga paged the team. A bug in the new code left root‑endpoint connections open, causing monitoring checks to time out and continue reporting failure even after the service was back up. The combination of unsilenced alerts and the connection leak resulted in prolonged false alarms.
mitigation_principle: Silence monitoring during deployments or coordinate with ops; ensure developers have proper permissions to silence alerts; improve monitoring configuration to avoid false positives; separate code and config deployments to prevent inconsistent state; avoid automatic restarts during deployment; improve UI clarity for alert silencing

original_source: Outage caused by failed SFP+ module on memcached server mc1009, leading to cascading failures despite partial mitigation via twemproxy deployment.
failure_pattern: A failed SFP+ module on the switch caused its EEPROM to become unreadable, triggering a reboot of the entire ethernet chassis subsystem. The reboot severed network connectivity to the memcached server mc1009, bringing that cache node down. The loss of a single memcached node blocked application servers and cascaded failures to other caching layers such as Squid and Varnish, leaving only cached pages available.
mitigation_principle: Distribute critical services across multiple switches and racks; implement redundancy and failover for network components; monitor hardware health and perform proactive replacement; use proxy layers like twemproxy to isolate failures; improve logging and statistics collection for proxies

original_source: Continuous Integration services fell over due to disk space issues and Gerrit replication failures.
failure_pattern: Disk space exhaustion on the Beta Jenkins master caused the job queue to stall, while Gerrit replication failures led to repeated re‑queuing of replication jobs that clogged Gerrit and blocked stream‑events, preventing Zuul from seeing changes and causing the CI services to fail.
mitigation_principle: implement disk space monitoring and alerts; add comprehensive monitoring for Gerrit, Jenkins, and Zuul; reduce replication retry aggressiveness; establish automated health checks for the CI pipeline; enforce capacity planning and capacity alerts

original_source: New user accounts not fully created due to VisualEditor A/B testing code
symptoms: new user accounts missing email and password
failure_pattern: The A/B testing sorting logic in VisualEditor incorrectly processed new account records, causing the email and password fields to be omitted. As a result, thousands of accounts were created in a partially initialized state, preventing users from logging in or receiving confirmation emails.
mitigation_principle: implement comprehensive unit tests for account creation logic; add automated monitoring and alerting for critical log events; enforce code review for A/B testing changes; maintain a dedicated log monitoring pipeline

original_source: Mail outage caused by spam-induced LDAP overload and misconfigured replication
root_cause_category: resource exhaustion due to misconfiguration and high load
failure_pattern: A misconfigured LDAP replication caused the LDAP server to attempt to replicate from a non‑existent host, leading to misdiagnosis and escalation. Spam backscatter from $random@wikimedia.org flooded the LDAP server with thousands of queries per second, exhausting its file descriptor limit and causing the listening socket to close. The resulting LDAP failure caused mail relays to queue and eventually overload the mail server, producing a widespread mail outage.
mitigation_principle: Correct replication configuration and remove hardcoded /etc/hosts entries; upgrade OpenDJ to a version with proper resource limits; add secondary LDAP for mail traffic; implement LDAP query paging and failover; set appropriate ulimit and monitor LDAP load; index LDAP attributes to reduce query latency; separate mail relay and list services to isolate failures

original_source: Site outage during deployment due to improperly deployed WikibaseDataModel extension causing mergeMessageFileList.php to abort
symptoms: error logs indicating invalid magic word
failure_pattern: During a deployment, the WikibaseDataModel extension was listed in extension‑list but its files were not properly checked out, causing mergeMessageFileList.php to abort when it attempted to load the missing extension. The abort propagated through the site’s initialization, leading to a complete outage. Subsequent attempts to fix the deployment introduced further errors, but the root issue was the incomplete deployment of the extension.
mitigation_principle: Ensure all referenced extensions are fully deployed before activation; add sanity checks in deployment scripts to verify file existence; implement graceful handling of missing extensions in mergeMessageFileList.php; use versioned deployment pipelines; document deployment procedures and communicate changes

original_source: Wikis using Wikibase on 1.22wmf11 experienced 40-minute outage due to fatal error on every Apache request.
symptoms: fatal error on every Apache request
failure_pattern: A bug in the Wikibase application on the 1.22wmf11 release triggered a fatal error on every Apache request. The error caused Apache to terminate or return 500 responses, rendering the wikis inaccessible for approximately 40 minutes.
mitigation_principle: implement comprehensive unit and integration tests for application code; enforce code review and static analysis; add robust error handling and graceful degradation; monitor application logs for fatal errors; perform staged rollouts and rollback procedures

original_source: ZeroRatedMobileAccess extension failure due to dependency on MobileFrontend after deployment
failure_pattern: The ZeroRatedMobileAccess extension was updated to use the MFResourceLoader module from MobileFrontend. After deployment, MobileFrontend was disabled on Wikidata, so Zero attempted to instantiate MFResourceLoader and could not find the class, causing fatal errors that resulted in pages rendering without styles or scripts.
mitigation_principle: Add guard checks to verify dependent extensions are enabled before activating ZeroRatedMobileAccess; allow a buffer period between deployments and monitor fatal errors; ensure deployment pipelines validate that all required dependencies are present

original_source: Parsoid cluster corrupted charset in wikitext due to broken deployment with busboy library
symptoms: non-ASCII characters corrupted in page content
failure_pattern: The deployment of Parsoid with the new busboy library introduced a default ISO-8859-1 encoding for POST data, causing incoming HTML containing non-ASCII characters to be misinterpreted and corrupted during conversion to wikitext. This resulted in VisualEditor edits being corrupted across wikis for approximately 55 minutes until the deployment was reverted.
mitigation_principle: explicitly configure encoding for third-party libraries; add end-to-end integration tests covering encoding; implement sanity checks on content size differences; enable rapid rollback of deployments; perform manual testing on non-English wikis before deployment

original_source: CirrusSearch outages from 16:00 to 20:00 UTC due to misconfigured redundancy, Elasticsearch upgrade issues, and LVS decommissioning errors
root_cause_category: misconfigured redundancy and partial upgrade causing data loss
failure_pattern: The cluster was configured with zero replicas, making it vulnerable to node failures. During a rolling upgrade, nodes ran mixed Elasticsearch 0.90.4 and 0.90.7 versions, and a manual disk wipe on a node removed shard copies. This caused shards to become unassigned, triggering Elasticsearch to enter a red state and leading to search and update failures across wikis.
mitigation_principle: automated redundancy verification; enforce single-version upgrades; use automated cluster health monitoring; avoid manual data directory wipes; ensure load balancer updates; maintain fallback search engine

original_source: Data loss in Labs home directories due to erroneous Puppet symlink
failure_pattern: Puppet automatically upgraded rsyslog, which restarted the service and caused Swift to lose its syslog socket. Swift entered a busy loop logging errors, became overloaded, and cascaded failures to the imagescaler cluster, rendering it unresponsive and triggering critical alerts.
mitigation_principle: avoid automatic package upgrades for critical services; implement dependency checks before upgrades; monitor service restarts and validate downstream impact; use canary deployments; add health checks for syslog connectivity

original_source: PoolCounter errors and page display issues on jawiki and ruwiki due to CategoryTree extension change
symptoms: anonymous users receiving PoolCounter error messages
page display issues on jawiki and ruwiki
failure_pattern: An update to the CategoryTree extension increased the load on page parsing, causing the poolcounter queues to fill and block page rendering. The resulting queue overflow produced PoolCounter error messages and prevented pages such as the Main Page from being displayed to anonymous users.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated regression testing for extensions; monitor performance metrics after changes; enforce code review for performance impact; add monitoring for poolcounter service; use feature flags or rollback strategy; improve error handling and user-friendly messages

original_source: Overload of Bits application servers due to change in default JavaScript and CSS payload caused loss of CSS and JavaScript for some users.
symptoms: pages loading without styling and interactivity
failure_pattern: A change to the default JavaScript and CSS payload increased the load on the Bits application servers, causing them to overload and generate socket timeouts. The overloaded servers could not serve the static assets, resulting in pages being delivered without CSS or JavaScript for users.
mitigation_principle: Deploy payload changes in a staggered fashion; add redundancy to application cluster; implement load testing and monitoring; use feature flags for gradual rollout; ensure graceful degradation of missing assets

original_source: A bad Puppet change regarding sysctl & RP filtering broke LVS balancers and went undetected until a large scale outage.
failure_pattern: A Puppet change lowered the priority of sysctl rp_filter settings, causing Ubuntu's default sysctl to re‑enable rp_filter after reboot. The re‑enabled rp_filter blocked asymmetric routing on LVS balancers, preventing internal traffic from reaching backend services. This resulted in 503 errors for HTTPS and failures of internal services while external traffic appeared fine.
mitigation_principle: monitor critical sysctl parameters; include internal service tests in failover validation; ensure configuration changes set correct priority and are reviewed for impact on critical components; deploy wide changes incrementally on critical systems

original_source: Cache stampede caused by parser cache key change for pages with math due to Gerrit change 104991
root_cause_category: cache key change causing cache stampede
failure_pattern: The Gerrit change 104991 altered the parser cache keys for pages containing <math>, causing many previously cached pages to miss the cache. The sudden surge in cache misses triggered a cache stampede, overwhelming the cluster and leading to Apache HTTP timeouts and service downtime.
mitigation_principle: implement thorough testing for cache key changes; use cache invalidation strategies; monitor cache hit rates; roll out changes gradually; enforce code review for caching changes; use pool counter to limit resource usage

original_source: Parsoid node disk exhaustion due to verbose logging and broken log rotation caused VisualEditor errors
failure_pattern: Broken log rotation allowed verbose logging to fill node disks, causing Parsoid processes to block on stdout/stderr and stop accepting requests; this resulted in connection refusals and VisualEditor errors for users.
mitigation_principle: implement hourly log rotation; monitor disk usage thresholds early; use asynchronous logging to avoid blocking; test log rotation and logging volume in CI; remove legacy init scripts and update documentation

original_source: CirrusSearch outage due to incomplete Puppet configuration on new Elasticsearch servers
failure_pattern: Puppet applied only half of the configuration to the new Elasticsearch nodes, omitting the JVM heap settings in /etc/default/elasticsearch. The nodes started with the default small heap, and when a large index migrated to them the heap filled, causing the JVM to spend all CPU time on garbage collection. This blocked search queries, caused timeouts, and eventually made the application unresponsive.
mitigation_principle: Ensure complete configuration deployment for critical services; monitor slow query logs and error counts; add appropriate timeouts to client requests; set proper JVM heap sizes; avoid simultaneous restarts of clustered services; use configuration management validation before applying changes

original_source: API latency spike caused by Pybal DNS misconfiguration after server renumbering
failure_pattern: The renumbering of API servers required DNS changes, but Pybal did not update its backend IP list, leaving stale IPs in rotation. Requests were routed to unreachable servers, causing timeouts and high latency, which propagated to Parsoid and Varnish, resulting in slow page loads for users.
mitigation_principle: implement automated DNS change detection in load balancers; enforce removal of decommissioned servers from load balancer config; add health checks and error logging; create alerts for unusual API latency; test load balancer after network changes

original_source: Partial outage due to scap deployment failures on servers in row D caused by missing rsync permissions and configuration issues.
symptoms: fatal PHP errors due to missing /usr/local/apache/common-local/php-1.23wmf18/api.php
wikis in group0 (test* and mw.o) unavailable for ~25 minutes
missing localization messages on affected hosts
root_cause_category: configuration error (missing rsync permissions and host allow list)
failure_pattern: The scap deployment attempted to rsync new PHP code to servers in row D, but the rsync slave hosts lacked the necessary permissions and host‑allow entries for the new row. Consequently the php-1.23wmf18 directory was never created on those servers, leading to fatal PHP errors and missing localization data. The incomplete state caused a partial outage of the affected wikis until the missing directories were manually synced and caches rebuilt.
mitigation_principle: Ensure rsync permissions and host‑allow lists are managed by puppet; validate rsync sync success before proceeding; add automated checks for missing directories and missing files; document procedures for moving servers between rows; monitor scap logs for sync failures; enforce consistency of deployment tooling across environments

original_source: EventLogging writer shutdown due to database connection failures on db1047
failure_pattern: The database server db1047 stopped accepting connections after a crash or manual restart, causing the EventLogging writer to repeatedly fail to connect. The upstart job hit its failure threshold and stopped respawning the writer, resulting in no EventLogging data and blank reports. An Icinga alert was triggered but not responded to, delaying remediation.
mitigation_principle: Separate analytics workloads from other database traffic; clarify alert ownership and response times; move EventLogging database to a dedicated server; ensure database replication and failover; monitor database health and alert thresholds; automate respawn or restart on failure

original_source: DB user misconfiguration due to changes in PrivateSettings.php causing jobs to run under incorrect user
symptoms: jobs running under incorrect DB user
maintenance scripts failing due to user mismatch
failure_pattern: A change to PrivateSettings.php removed references to AdminSettings.php, causing the DB user settings to default to the wrong user (wikiuser) instead of the intended wikiadmin. Because the file was not in version control, the change went unnoticed until the next scheduled scap, leading to jobs executing under the wrong user and producing broken dumps and failed maintenance scripts.
mitigation_principle: Keep all configuration files in version control; enforce code review and immediate deployment for critical config changes; coordinate changes across dependent systems; implement monitoring to detect unexpected user or permission changes

original_source: Failure in ExtensionMessages-wmfNN.php generation during l10nupdate caused recurring site breaks
failure_pattern: During the nightly l10nupdate, the ExtensionMessages-wmfNN.php files were not regenerated at the correct time, causing new JSON localization files to be omitted from the site. This omission prevented the site from loading localized content, resulting in site breaks. The issue recurred each time the nightly job ran until the generation process was fixed.
mitigation_principle: Add automated tests to verify PHP message file generation after l10nupdate; enforce build pipeline to run generation before deployment; monitor for missing message files; implement rollback on generation failure; document and review regeneration steps for new extensions

original_source: MediaWiki configuration incorrectly throttled media servers due to untrusted X-Forwarded-For headers
component: MediaWiki throttle configuration / trusted proxy setting
symptoms: rate limit error messages to users
failure_pattern: The MediaWiki throttle logic applied to the media server IPs because the X‑Forwarded‑For header was not trusted. As a result, the system treated the proxy IPs as end users and throttled them, causing thumbnail generation failures for all users.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated validation of trusted proxy lists; add monitoring and alerts for unexpected throttle spikes; enforce code review and documentation for proxy configuration changes; maintain configuration drift detection; schedule regular audits of proxy trust settings

original_source: Data loss in EventLogging due to CPU-bound validation on Vanadium from 5/09 to 6/06
failure_pattern: The EventLogging service on Vanadium validated incoming events against a JSON schema. The validation code was CPU-intensive, causing the CPU to max out and limiting throughput to ~250 events/s. As a result, events that could not be validated within the time window were dropped, leading to data loss observed by users.
mitigation_principle: implement throughput monitoring and alerts; optimize validation logic to reduce CPU usage; apply rate limiting or backpressure; notify users of data loss; avoid frequent schema validation

original_source: Memcached failure on mw1151 due to disk issues caused cache misses and broken ResourceLoader functionality
symptoms: increased server load due to cache misses
ResourceLoader modules timestamp renewal causing no memory of previous version
Gadgets and other extensions disabled due to cache failure
root_cause_category: disk hardware failure leading to memcached outage
failure_pattern: Disk errors on mw1151 caused the memcached service to become disabled, preventing caching of ResourceLoader definitions and gadget definitions. This resulted in cache misses, increased computation, and modules not loading for users.
mitigation_principle: Implement disk health monitoring and alerts; enable automatic memcached failover and load balancing; isolate and decommission failing nodes; use redundant storage and regular hardware checks; set up health checks to remove sick nodes from load balancer

original_source: MySQL process killed by OOM on db1001 due to traffic spike affecting multiple services
symptoms: services down (bacula, blog, bugzilla, civicrm, etherpad, puppet, racktables, rt)
failure_pattern: A sudden traffic spike increased MySQL connections, queries, and memory usage on db1001, causing mysqld to exceed its memory limits; the kernel OOM killer terminated the mysqld process, leading to database downtime and subsequent InnoDB crash recovery, while MyISAM tables failed to start and required manual repair.
mitigation_principle: Implement per-user connection limits; migrate MyISAM tables to InnoDB or ARIA; monitor memory usage and set OOM alerts; enforce proper query sampling and increase sample rates; use Elasticsearch for fulltext search; scale database resources to handle traffic spikes

original_source: Service disruption due to removal of wikimedia-task-appserver package causing loss of critical symlinks and user deletion
failure_pattern: The removal of the wikimedia-task-appserver package executed a post‑removal script that deleted the mwdeploy user and unlinked critical symlinks (/etc/apache2/wmf and /usr/local/apache/common). These symlinks contained Apache configuration files, so Apache lost its DocumentRoot and Directory directives, resulting in 404 responses that were cached in Varnish and caused a sustained spike in 4xx traffic.
mitigation_principle: Validate package post‑removal scripts before deployment; ensure critical users and symlinks are not deleted by package removal; puppetize all critical symlinks; perform pre‑removal impact analysis; enforce idempotent configuration management; implement cache invalidation strategy for Varnish after configuration changes

original_source: Search slowdown and temporary errors due to Elasticsearch node performance issues
failure_pattern: An old geo box node (elastic1017) was added to the Elasticsearch cluster, causing high I/O wait as it restored shards. The resulting disk thrashing slowed query execution, leading to search slowdown and temporary errors for users. Removing the node immediately restored performance.
mitigation_principle: Deploy nodes with adequate I/O capacity; monitor disk I/O and node health; avoid adding nodes during peak load or on Friday afternoons; implement automatic health checks to detect and isolate sick nodes; use SSDs for search nodes; schedule maintenance outside business hours

original_source: Data loss in Kafka due to disk failure on analytics1021 and insufficient capacity on single broker
root_cause_category: hardware failure causing single point of failure
failure_pattern: A disk failure on analytics1021 caused a read‑only filesystem, leading the Kafka broker to shut down. The broker’s partitions were reassigned to the remaining broker, but that broker lacked sufficient capacity to handle the full traffic load, resulting in dropped messages and data loss.
mitigation_principle: implement redundant disk configurations (RAID), increase broker capacity, monitor disk health, add more brokers, automate failover, avoid single-broker deployments, perform load testing, use alerting for disk I/O errors

original_source: Video processing stopped due to unsynchronized job-loop script change on videoscalers
failure_pattern: An update to the job-loop bash script introduced an unused argument that was not removed from the videoscaler puppet manifests. Puppet detected the change and restarted the videoscaler service, but the modified script failed to launch jobs correctly, causing video conversion to halt. Users observed that newly uploaded videos were not being processed.
mitigation_principle: Add automated tests for script changes; implement monitoring and alerts for job status; synchronize configuration changes across all nodes; enhance job-loop logging and error handling

original_source: Lsearchd-based search instability leads to migration plan towards ElasticSearch.
failure_pattern: The lsearchd process entered a deadlock, causing both members of search pool 4 to become unresponsive. Monitoring via pybal only reported the failure after the pool was down, leading to a 30‑minute recovery cycle. During this time users received empty search results or errors.
mitigation_principle: replace legacy lsearchd with ElasticSearch; improve and update documentation; add comprehensive health checks beyond pybal; implement automated restarts and deadlock detection; decommission unstable components

original_source: Wikitech downtime due to puppet and Apache configuration issues
failure_pattern: Puppet catalog compilation failed due to a duplicate package definition, preventing puppet from applying updates. During the outage, an Apache refactor added a conflicting sites‑enabled file; when Apache restarted it selected the wrong virtual host, redirecting traffic to virt1000 and rendering Wikitech unusable until manual patches were applied.
mitigation_principle: Add monitoring for puppet run failures; trigger alerts on configuration errors; validate configuration changes with automated tests before merging; enforce idempotent package definitions; implement fallback defaults for critical services; review and test refactor patches in staging before production

original_source: EventLogging system overwhelmed by high event volume from MobileWebSearch schema, causing data loss and service disruption.
root_cause_category: capacity overload leading to buffer overflow
failure_pattern: A sudden surge of 500 events per second from the MobileWebSearch schema exceeded the EventLogging system’s capacity. The ZMQ buffer overflowed, causing the consumer process to be killed for excessive memory usage, which in turn led to 40% event loss and four data gaps.
mitigation_principle: implement dynamic or anomaly‑based volume alarms; migrate to a more robust transport layer such as Kafka; increase buffer capacity and scale EventLogging components; monitor per‑schema throughput and adjust thresholds hourly

original_source: Mailman outage due to configuration patch causing unexpected issues during maintenance window
symptoms: messages held for moderation even when sender is a list member
failure_pattern: A configuration patch was merged and deployed without restarting Mailman. During the maintenance window the service was restarted, triggering errors caused by the patch. mitigation_principle: Require service restart on configuration change; test configuration changes in staging before production; centralize logs for all services; provide non-ops access to logs; use automated rollback for failed patches

original_source: RESTBase service outage due to parallel Puppet execution during Cassandra keyspace creation
symptoms: users unable to access VE, OCG, CXServer
failure_pattern: Parallel Puppet agents restarted RESTBase nodes simultaneously, causing concurrent attempts to create new Cassandra keyspaces. Cassandra cannot handle parallel keyspace/table creation, leading to timeouts and service unavailability. The cluster remained down until keyspaces were manually removed and services restarted sequentially.
mitigation_principle: disable automatic restarts during deployment; perform rolling restarts; ensure sequential keyspace creation; monitor Cassandra keyspace creation; automate deployment pipeline to handle distributed services

original_source: Performance degradation and 503 errors due to cookie name change in MediaWiki 1.26wmf7 affecting Varnish caching
failure_pattern: The deployment of MediaWiki 1.26wmf7 introduced new cookie names that matched Varnish’s session‑cookie regex, causing Varnish to bypass caching for all requests. The revert did not immediately resolve the issue because the destructive cookies remained in users’ browsers, so the problem persisted until a Varnish‑level fix removed the cookie from the regex.
mitigation_principle: Require ops review of any cookie changes that affect caching; enforce automated tests for caching behavior on new cookie names; document and enforce deployment checklist for localization cache validation; enable selective version rollback to isolate problematic releases

original_source: GridEngine master failure due to oversized /etc/hosts file after package upgrade
symptoms: no new jobs could be started
root_cause_category: configuration corruption due to oversized /etc/hosts file
failure_pattern: The package upgrade triggered a restart of the GridEngine master, but the oversized /etc/hosts file caused the GridEngine gethostbyname routine to fail, preventing hostname resolution and causing the master daemon to crash and refuse to restart. original_source: Data loss in tagging data due to emergency changes deployed on 2015-05-22
failure_pattern: An emergency change was deployed on 2015-05-22 that altered the tagging data ingestion configuration, causing the system to stop capturing tagging data. The loss was unrecoverable because the data had already been discarded, leading to a permanent loss of tagging information.

original_source: Redis slaves rdb1002 and rdb1004 unable to sync from master after restart, affecting OCG, job queue, and other services
symptoms: services unable to read from Redis slaves
failure_pattern: After upgrading and restarting Redis, the output buffer limits for slave clients were too low, causing the slaves to fail to sync from the master. This replication lag led to OCG sporadic 500 errors and job queue failures as services attempted to read from unsynced slaves.

original_source: NFS server outage on labstore1001 due to switch errors and network connectivity issues
failure_pattern: The switch experienced a series of errors that corrupted its MAC table and caused link flapping, which in turn severed network connectivity for labstore1001 and other hosts. The loss of connectivity forced the NFS server to become unreachable, leading to high CPU usage, file descriptor exhaustion, and a prolonged outage.

original_source: HTTP service outage in esams due to LVS healthcheck failure after enwiki HTTPS transition
symptoms: HTTP requests failed for primary text services
failure_pattern: The LVS healthcheck for HTTP traffic pointed to a URL that began redirecting to HTTPS after the enwiki HTTPS transition, causing healthchecks to fail. Pybal’s depool_threshold logic left half of the backends depooled, but when a server list change was applied the threshold was bypassed, so all backends were marked depooled and removed from the IPVS configuration, resulting in a complete HTTP outage.

original_source: Elasticsearch outage causing partial and full search unavailability for 6 and 3 hours respectively due to cluster instability and monitoring deficiencies.
root_cause_category: cluster instability caused by node failures and garbage collection stalls
failure_pattern: Node failures and prolonged garbage collection on several ES hosts caused the master nodes to become unresponsive, leading to shard failures and a cluster that remained in a yellow/green state but did not trigger alerts. Search requests routed to the cluster failed, producing 5xx errors and user‑facing search unavailability for several hours.
mitigation_principle: Improve monitoring to detect GC stalls and cluster health; separate master and data nodes; implement graceful degradation and circuit breakers; use statsd plugin for metrics; automate node restarts and health checks; tune GC settings; decouple search traffic; enforce stricter configuration validation

original_source: Elasticsearch service partially down for 85 minutes and fully unavailable for 30 minutes due to cluster node failures.
failure_pattern: Multiple Elasticsearch nodes failed starting at 04:35 UTC, causing a cluster partition even though the master node remained online. The partition prevented search nodes from rejoining the cluster, leading to partial service degradation and eventually a full outage when search was disabled. original_source: Data loss in Labs home directories due to catastrophic NFS filesystem failure and subsequent restoration from backup
failure_pattern: The NFS filesystem backing the Labs storage suffered corruption—likely due to hardware or configuration issues—causing the kernel to remount it read‑only. This prevented write access for all dependent services, leading to an NFS outage and widespread service disruption. Recovery required restoring from backup, which extended downtime.
mitigation_principle: implement configuration management for storage systems; shard NFS servers to eliminate single points of failure; reduce filesystem size to speed backups; fix hardware issues promptly; establish a clear, tested backup and restore plan; simplify NFS configuration; reduce reliance on NFS for non‑essential services

original_source: Server side events were dropped due to missing --count flag in forwarder config during deployment.
failure_pattern: During deployment, the --count flag was omitted from the server side forwarder configuration. Without this flag, the forwarder did not process incoming events, causing all server side events to be dropped for the duration of the outage.

original_source: RESTBase workers stuck due to Cassandra query timeouts and failed automatic restarts on 2015-07-02
symptoms: connections refused on RESTBase load balancer
RESTBase workers stuck due to Cassandra query timeouts
failure_pattern: High load on the Cassandra cluster caused query timeouts, which in turn caused RESTBase workers to hang. The stuck workers prevented new connections from being accepted, leading to connection refusals on the load balancer. Automatic worker restarts failed to recover the service.

original_source: Data loss in Kafka cluster during upgrade due to insufficient testing with varnishkafka and live event streams
failure_pattern: During the upgrade, partitions were reassigned from older 0.8.1.1 brokers to newer 0.8.2.1 brokers; the lack of testing with varnishkafka and live event streams caused metadata requests to time out, leading to failed produce requests and subsequent data loss.

original_source: Firewall change on helium caused conntrack table overflow and API outage due to failed ferm service

original_source: Kafka upgrade incident due to snappy-java bug causing data bloat and replication issues during 0.8.2.1 migration

original_source: Nova services flapping in Labs due to suspected RabbitMQ and nova-network failure

original_source: HHVM FastStringSearch extension removal caused fatal errors and configuration mishandling led to site outage.

original_source: Grid engine exec daemon failed to restart after reboots, causing Tool Labs webservice outages
root_cause_category: boot failure causing daemon not start
failure_pattern: The gridengine-exec daemon failed to start on reboot of exec nodes, leaving those nodes offline. The queue became overloaded and jobs could not be scheduled, causing webservice outages for Tool Labs. Lack of monitoring and documentation delayed detection and resolution.

original_source: OCSP Stapling issue causing HTTPS connectivity problems for Firefox users due to GlobalSign response failures and inadequate validation in updater process.
symptoms: HTTPS connectivity problems for Firefox users
browser errors indicating invalid signing certificate
intermittent full failures on direct OCSP queries
intermittent failures in browsers despite OCSP stapling disabled
failure_pattern: GlobalSign sent OCSP responses with expired or nearly‑expired signatures and occasional "trylater" replies; the OCSP Updater only checked the NotBefore/NotAfter window and ignored signature expiry, so it accepted these invalid responses and stapled them to HTTPS responses, causing browsers—especially Firefox—to reject the connections; intermittent failures persisted until a manual workaround replaced the bad responses.
mitigation_principle: implement comprehensive OCSP response validation including signature expiry; handle non‑successful OCSP responses gracefully; enable automatic updates only after successful validation; monitor OCSP response health and alert on anomalies; provide fallback to direct OCSP queries if stapled response is invalid

original_source: MediaWiki patch caused IP address leakage in recent changes log during category updates via purge API
symptoms: IP addresses of editors leaked in recent changes log
privacy violation due to IP leakage
root_cause_category: design oversight leading to IP leakage
failure_pattern: A patch to MediaWiki’s category update logic incorrectly used a function that returned the IP of the caller, causing purge API calls to be logged with the caller’s IP instead of the editor’s. original_source: Surge in Cirrus Elastica Write jobs caused Redis memory and disk exhaustion, leading to jobqueue and OCX malfunction.

original_source: Elasticsearch service disruption due to firewall rule application on master node

original_source: ORES service downtime during upgrade due to incorrect version deployment and pip inefficiencies
failure_pattern: An outdated master branch was pushed to the deploy branch, causing the wrong version of ORES to be deployed. The service could not start, leading to a two‑hour outage. Additionally, pip attempted to reinstall packages unnecessarily, adding deployment time.

original_source: Network outage in Labs due to kernel failure on labnet1002 and monitoring misconfiguration.

original_source: Performance degradation and user skin preference loss due to database cleanup on enwiki and smaller wikis

failure_pattern: The cleanup script executed a DELETE without using the primary key, causing a full scan of 17 million rows on the master. original_source: Graphite overwhelmed by legitimate requests from misbehaving dashboards causing 500 errors

original_source: Network outage caused by Equinix customer's IPv6 flood and MPLS link amplification triggering BGP routing loop

original_source: rsyslog config change caused Swift outage leading to partial public outage on upload.wikimedia.org image fetches

original_source: Service disruption during cxserver service-runner migration due to incomplete testing and monitoring

original_source: Payment processing degraded due to MySQL table open cache exhaustion

original_source: MediaWiki 1.27.0-wmf.11 reverted due to SessionManager-related logout and session handling issues

Login failures on Android app and meta wikis

original_source: Kafka node disk exhaustion due to unrotated GC logs causing EventLogging processor disconnections

original_source: MediaWiki API cluster failure due to Kafka broker reboot causing connection overload
failure_pattern: A scheduled kernel upgrade caused a reboot of Kafka broker kafka1012, abruptly removing it from the cluster. Clients attempted to reconnect, creating a surge of SYN_SENT connections that overloaded the broker and the application, leading to socket timeouts and API failures across the MediaWiki cluster.
mitigation_principle: Implement graceful shutdown procedures for critical services during maintenance; enforce connection retry limits and backoff strategies; monitor and limit SYN_SENT connection backlog; use circuit breakers and health checks to isolate failing components; perform rolling restarts to avoid simultaneous outages; add redundancy and load balancing for critical brokers

original_source: Data loss in /srv/mediawiki-staging on mira due to incorrect sync during tin reimage
root_cause_category: human error during server reimage causing incorrect sync
failure_pattern: The reimage of tin triggered a sync-master between tin and mira before tin was fully provisioned, causing scap-master-sync to run from mira to tin and wiping /srv/mediawiki-staging on mira. This data loss led to mediawiki failures until the directory was rebuilt from scratch.
mitigation_principle: implement sanity checks and confirmation prompts in sync scripts; enforce two‑stage pooling to separate sync‑from and sync‑to states; include all critical directories in backups; audit and limit untracked files; improve operator coordination and communication

original_source: Phabricator downtime due to incorrect Puppet configuration after server reboot
failure_pattern: A server reboot cleared a non‑persistent lock file in /var/run, allowing Puppet to run and update Phabricator repositories to mismatched tags; the service then failed. A manual fix restored the correct tags, but Puppet ran again before the lock file was recreated, reverting the repos to the broken state. An Apache graceful restart cleared the opcode cache, exposing the mismatched code and causing the outage.
mitigation_principle: Use persistent lock files or idempotent deployment mechanisms; protect critical configuration changes with persistent state; implement automated tests to detect repo tag drift; replace hard‑coded Puppet tags with a deployment tool like scap3; add monitoring for repo state consistency; document and enforce reboot maintenance procedures

original_source: Scheduled maintenance on February 9th, 2016 caused a temporary read-only mode for several wikis during hardware, OS, and database upgrades.
failure_pattern: During the scheduled maintenance window, the wiki edit service was put into read‑only mode to allow hardware, OS, and database upgrades. The upgrade process took longer than anticipated, keeping the service in read‑only mode until 23:30 UTC instead of the planned 5‑minute window, which caused edit failures for users during that period.
mitigation_principle: accurate maintenance scheduling; automated monitoring of read‑only mode duration; staged rollouts; clear communication of maintenance windows; use of health checks to detect failures early

original_source: MediaWiki deployment outage due to incorrect file sync order causing HHVM fatal errors
root_cause_category: operator error: incorrect file sync order
failure_pattern: During a deployment to backport a logging enhancement, the deployer synced files in the wrong order, updating Setup.php before SessionManager.php. This left the codebase in an inconsistent state where SessionManager lacked the checkIpLimits method, causing HHVM fatal errors for all requests. The error propagated across all wikis, resulting in a 2.5 minute outage.
mitigation_principle: use canary deployments; implement rolling deploys; add automated error detection and abort mechanisms; prepare sync-file statements ahead of time; enforce strict deployment order; perform pre-deployment validation

original_source: Lax sudo policies in Labs instances due to keystone migration error
failure_pattern: During the keystone migration, the migration script recreated Labs projects and inadvertently re‑applied the default sudo policies, granting global sudo and sudo‑as privileges. This misconfiguration allowed unrestricted sudo usage across the labs instances, leading to a potential security breach. The issue was later detected, global sudo rules were removed, and the original restrictive policies were restored.
mitigation_principle: Implement negative permission tests; Automate policy validation post‑migration; Centralize and audit sudo policy changes; Move auth logs to central logging; Write tests to monitor login and sudo permissions

original_source: Disk failure on labsdb1002 causes unmount of tools databases, requiring depooling and manual recovery steps.
failure_pattern: A physical disk failure on labsdb1002 triggered I/O errors that caused the XFS filesystem to shut down and unmount /srv, leading to the crash of mysqld processes and the unavailability of the tools databases. The failure forced the database server to be depooled, requiring manual recovery steps and a temporary redirect of traffic to other shards.
mitigation_principle: replace failed disks promptly; implement automatic failover for database shards; monitor disk health and I/O errors proactively; use redundant storage or RAID to avoid single disk failure; automate depooling and service restart

original_source: ORES went down and responded slowly for  2 hours today.
failure_pattern: During deployment, pip installed new wheels without removing old versions, filling the environment and causing resource exhaustion. The overloaded environment led to ORES becoming unresponsive and slow for two hours. Additionally, the precaching utility resumed after a brief outage, generating a burst of requests that further stressed the service.
mitigation_principle: implement automated version purging for pip installs; enforce clean environment before deployment; add load testing for precaching utility; add node scaling; monitor disk usage; use immutable deployment images

original_source: All Mediawiki servers were serving mostly HTTP 5XX for about 5 minutes at 1350 UTC due to a buggy configuration during CirrusSearch traffic switch to codfw.
failure_pattern: A buggy configuration was applied when switching CirrusSearch traffic to the codfw datacenter, causing the Mediawiki servers to misroute or mishandle requests and return HTTP 5XX errors for about five minutes until the change was rolled back.
mitigation_principle: implement automated canary testing for configuration changes; standardize and automate configuration validation; test configuration changes on dedicated test nodes before production

original_source: Performance degradation and HTTP 502 errors in WDQS due to Blazegraph bug and Jolokia file descriptor leak
root_cause_category: resource exhaustion due to file descriptor leak
failure_pattern: A bug in Blazegraph caused deadlocks and high latency, while the Jolokia monitoring agent leaked file descriptors, exhausting system resources. The combined effect slowed the Wikidata Query Service, leading Varnish to return HTTP 502 errors to users.
mitigation_principle: run monitoring agents as Java agents to avoid FD leaks; add application-level response time checks; deploy updated database versions to fix known bugs; scale out nodes during maintenance; enhance monitoring for early detection

original_source: Feedback loop in ChangeProp test deploy caused overload of RESTBase and Parsoid clusters
failure_pattern: A misconfigured ChangeProp test deployment propagated un-cacheable requests to RESTBase and Parsoid, creating a feedback loop that repeatedly hit those services. The resulting overload of RESTBase and Parsoid clusters caused high latency and request errors for users.
mitigation_principle: Implement concurrency limiting on change propagation; avoid following redirects; enforce cache-control headers; rate limit repeated parses; add functional cluster checks

original_source: Elasticsearch slowdown due to large segment merge and garbage collection issues on elastic1026.
root_cause_category: resource exhaustion due to large segment merge and garbage collection
failure_pattern: A large segment merge on elastic1026 triggered intensive garbage collection cycles, which consumed excessive CPU resources. The resulting CPU saturation caused Elasticsearch queries to experience high latency, leading to a slowdown in search response times.
mitigation_principle: Enable detailed GC logging for analysis; monitor GC and CPU metrics; tune segment merge settings to limit large merges; set alerts for high CPU and GC activity; consider scaling cluster or adding nodes to distribute load; review JVM GC configuration and adjust thresholds.

original_source: Incomplete deploy of toollabs webservice package caused restarts to fail proxy registration, leading to 90-minute outage.
failure_pattern: An incomplete deployment of the toollabs webservice package left some nodes running an older version that omitted the required --register-proxy flag. When webservices were restarted—by webservicemonitor or manual restarts—the new runner script executed without the flag, causing the services to lose proxy registration and become unreachable, resulting in a 90‑minute outage.
mitigation_principle: implement a robust deployment system; enforce version consistency across nodes; enable automated alerts for puppet failures; reduce dependency on NFS for critical services; improve monitoring and paging for webservice outages

original_source: Wikilabels service disruptions due to untested CORS changes
root_cause_category: CORS misconfiguration due to untested changes
failure_pattern: A new CORS configuration was deployed without adequate testing, causing browsers to reject cross‑origin requests. This prevented authentication cookies from being sent and blocked write actions, which in turn made it impossible for users to request worksets or assign tasks.
mitigation_principle: Implement comprehensive testing for configuration changes; add automated CI tests for CORS and OAuth; enforce code review and staging validation before production; ensure cross‑origin policies are validated with real clients

original_source: Deployment failure in CentralNotice due to missing submodule update during wmf.4 patch application
failure_pattern: A patch intended for wmf.4 was deployed without updating the required git submodule, leaving the CentralNotice code in an inconsistent state. The missing submodule update caused the bug to remain active, resulting in CentralNotice failures and broken notifications for users.
mitigation_principle: Implement a deployment checklist that includes verifying submodule updates; automate post‑deployment verification tests; require confirmation that all intended patches are present before marking a deploy complete; schedule major upgrades to avoid overlapping with critical maintenance windows; enforce peer review of deployment scripts

original_source: Mediawiki servers served HTTP 5xx for 101 seconds due to a typo in SpamBlacklist configuration during a SWAT deployment.
failure_pattern: A typo in the SpamBlacklist configuration caused the extension.json file to be referenced incorrectly, leading to a PHP fatal error on MediaWiki servers. This error propagated to HTTP 5xx responses for 101 seconds until the change was reverted.
mitigation_principle: implement automated configuration validation checks; add unit tests for configuration changes; enforce code review for configuration changes; use canary deployments to a small subset before full rollout; automate sync to test environment before production

original_source: Broken clamav update prevented mail delivery on ticket.wikimedia.org for 11 hours
failure_pattern: The new ClamAV package deprecated a configuration option that was still present in the puppet‑managed configuration. Because of this mismatch, clamd and freshclam refused to start, causing the OTRS mail delivery service to be unable to process the mail queue for about 11 hours. Removing the deprecated option allowed the services to start and mail delivery resumed.
mitigation_principle: Add monitoring checks for critical services; validate configuration changes before deployment; ensure backward compatibility of configuration options; implement automated tests for service start after updates; use configuration drift detection

original_source: CI infrastructure outage due to unrecoverable RAID failure on gallium.wikimedia.org
root_cause_category: hardware disk failure causing RAID corruption
failure_pattern: A disk failure on gallium.wikimedia.org caused the RAID array to become corrupted and the filesystem to mount read‑only, which in turn prevented Jenkins and Zuul from operating and caused the entire CI infrastructure to go down.
mitigation_principle: implement regular backups; replace aging hardware before failure; use redundant Jenkins masters; monitor SMART health; schedule controlled reboots with puppet; upgrade to newer OS releases

original_source: ORES downtime due to broken configuration file (99-redis.yaml) in puppet production branch
failure_pattern: A malformed 99-redis.yaml file was merged into the production branch of the puppet repository, causing puppet to apply an incorrect configuration to the Redis workers that ORES relies on. The misconfiguration prevented the workers from serving requests, resulting in 503 errors and timeouts for users for several hours until the file was removed and the workers were restarted.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated linting and validation for puppet manifests; enforce mandatory code review and testing before merging to production; add automated monitoring for configuration drift and service health; establish alerting for prolonged service degradation; maintain a rollback plan for puppet changes

original_source: ores.wikimedia.org was down for about twenty minutes due to deploying a commit that changed reading config directory without proper order.
failure_pattern: A commit that altered the order in which the ORES service reads its configuration directories caused the service to load incorrect settings. This misconfiguration prevented the uwsgi and celery workers from starting correctly, resulting in the ORES website being unavailable for about twenty minutes.
mitigation_principle: Implement safe deployment procedures; document configuration changes; enforce configuration validation; use automated tests for config changes; maintain rollback plan; separate config from code; use version control for config; perform staged rollouts

original_source: Etherpad downtime due to database corruption led to restoration from a one-day-old snapshot, resulting in potential data loss.
failure_pattern: A corruption in the etherpad database caused the ueberDB component to crash, leading to the etherpad-lite service terminating. The service remained down until a restore from a one‑day‑old snapshot was performed, resulting in loss of recent pad data.
mitigation_principle: implement robust per‑table backup strategy; enable continuous replication monitoring and validation; add automated database integrity health checks; enforce failover procedures with pre‑validation; provide rapid data recovery procedures for recent changes

original_source: Downtime of WDQS service due to symlink loss during Scap3 deployment migration
root_cause_category: missing symlink due to deployment tool misconfiguration
failure_pattern: During migration to Scap3 the application directory was replaced by a symlink, causing the symlink to the blazegraph data file (wikidata.jnl) to be lost. The missing symlink prevented WDQS from accessing its data, leading to service failure for about 20 minutes until the symlink was manually restored.
mitigation_principle: Use canaries for all deployments; ensure deployment tools preserve required symlinks; update puppet to avoid duplicate management of application directories; automate recreation of critical symlinks during deployment; document migration checklist with emphasis on canary usage

original_source: Commons database slaves replication failure leading to read-only mode and service disruption
symptoms: temporary impact on administrative actions on other wikis
root_cause_category: replication drift causing duplicate key errors
failure_pattern: An unsafe query or partially applied schema change on the master caused data drift, leading to duplicate key errors when slaves attempted to replicate. Replication halted, putting Commons into read‑only mode and disabling edits. A manual failover to a new master was performed, but mis‑configured binlog_format and remaining schema drift caused further replication failures, extending the outage until a fully consistent slave was promoted and the API and recentchanges services recovered.
mitigation_principle: Automate failover without code deploy; enforce consistent binlog_format across masters and slaves; implement automated drift detection and remediation; maintain schema consistency on all nodes; avoid unsafe queries; use GTID replication; monitor replication health; use etcd-controlled pooling

original_source: i18n messages not deployed properly for Echo due to disk space issues and cache problems
symptoms: missing i18n messages in Echo notifications
noticeable user impact due to missing messages
root_cause_category: disk space exhaustion causing failed localization update and cache poisoning
failure_pattern: Disk space exhaustion on the terbium server caused the l10n update to fail, leaving the ResourceLoader cache with incomplete i18n messages. Subsequent requests were served by Varnish with a stale cache that referenced the broken version, resulting in missing messages in Echo notifications for users.
mitigation_principle: implement disk space monitoring and alerts; enforce log rotation to prevent disk exhaustion; ensure l10n update completes before cache invalidation; validate localization deployment across all servers before release; use cache invalidation strategies to avoid stale content

original_source: Echo bug caused account auto-creation failures leading to inconsistent CentralAuth state and login blocks
symptoms: users unable to log in to wikis
inconsistent account state reported by CentralAuth
error messages: 'Could not find local user data for {Username}@{wiki}'
root_cause_category: bug in Echo leading to failed CentralAuth auto-creation
failure_pattern: A bug in Echo triggered internal API requests to other wikis during notification count updates, which attempted to use CentralAuth to create accounts. Because CentralAuth was not fully initialized, the auto-creation failed, leaving CentralAuth with a record of an account that didn't exist locally. This inconsistent state caused PasswordPoliciesForUser to block logins on all wikis, leading to widespread login failures.
mitigation_principle: implement comprehensive error handling for cross-wiki authentication flows; add pre-checks for CentralAuth initialization; isolate feature flag changes to prevent cascading failures; enforce communication protocols for incident escalation; maintain a recurring bug tracking system

original_source: ContentTranslation extension exhausts SQL connections due to high volume of API requests from a single user
root_cause_category: request flood due to missing rate limiting
failure_pattern: A single user triggered thousands of rapid calls to the ContentTranslation draft‑saving API, exhausting the MariaDB connection pool. The database became unavailable for other extensions, causing unresponsive behavior across the platform. The absence of automatic request limiting allowed the flood to occur unchecked.
mitigation_principle: Implement request rate limiting; add monitoring for database connection usage; audit front‑end code for excessive API calls; deploy automated alerts for connection pool exhaustion; enforce user request quotas

original_source: 503 errors due to missing PoolCounterClient.php entry point in MediaWiki configuration
failure_pattern: A duplicate entry point for PoolCounterClient.php was removed from the MediaWiki configuration, but the configuration still referenced the missing file. PHP used include instead of require, so the missing file did not trigger a fatal error until PoolCounter was invoked during page rendering, causing intermittent 503 Service Unavailable errors for users.
mitigation_principle: implement automated configuration validation; enforce use of require for critical files; enable canary deployments with fatal error detection; perform beta testing for missing files; audit extension loading

original_source: Global renames left local accounts unattached due to mixed MediaWiki versions during rollout of 1.28.0-wmf.11
symptoms: local accounts left unattached after global rename
users unable to access their local wiki accounts after rename
failure_pattern: The rollout of 1.28.0-wmf.11 added logic to detach local accounts during a global rename and reattach them via LocalRenameUserJob. During the mixed‑version period, group2 wikis still ran older code that lacked the reattachment logic, so renamed users’ local accounts remained unattached. This caused users to lose access to their local wiki accounts until all wikis were updated to the new version.
mitigation_principle: Ensure all dependent components are updated simultaneously; perform thorough regression testing across all cluster nodes; implement version compatibility checks; use feature flags to isolate changes; enforce short rollout windows; maintain clear change communication; monitor for mismatched versions

original_source: ORES service outage during deployment due to redis password configuration and response format regression
failure_pattern: During the deployment a mis‑configured Redis password prevented the ORES service from authenticating to its cache, while a regression in the V1 response format caused runtime exceptions. The combination of failed cache access and malformed responses triggered fatal errors in the ORES extension, leading to a one‑hour outage.
mitigation_principle: implement automated configuration validation; add pre‑deployment tests for external dependencies; use feature flags for API format changes; perform regression testing on API contracts; ensure comprehensive monitoring and alerting for service health

original_source: CI outage due to Nodepool exceeding inode quota on Jenkins master
failure_pattern: Nodepool attempted to create new instances on the Jenkins master, but the master’s inode quota was already reached. The resulting quota error caused nodepool to stop functioning, which in turn made Zuul and the CI pipeline unresponsive, leading to a multi‑hour outage.
mitigation_principle: schedule regular cleanup of unused Jenkins config files; implement inode quota monitoring and alerts; enforce limits on nodepool instance creation; automate garbage collection of stale nodepool data; separate nodepool storage from Jenkins master; add redundancy for nodepool service

original_source: Migration of two extensions to wfLoadExtension() caused production issues due to lack of testing and Logstash visibility.
root_cause_category: lack of testing and insufficient monitoring visibility
failure_pattern: Migrating the Timeline and ContactPage extensions to wfLoadExtension() without any automated tests and without updating the production configuration introduced PHP warnings and errors that were not captured by Logstash. The missing visibility caused the errors to go unnoticed until manual investigation, leading to site errors and degraded user experience until the fixes were applied.
mitigation_principle: implement automated tests for extensions; enforce code review and testing before merging; improve monitoring to capture all HHVM warnings; separate deployment of incompatible changes; document and automate deployment steps

original_source: VipsScaler extension configuration merge caused incorrect JPEG thumbnail rendering during .14 rollout
symptoms: JPEG thumbnails displayed with horizontal grey lines
failure_pattern: The VipsScaler extension was converted to extension registration, causing its default configuration to be merged with MediaWiki’s WMF configuration instead of overriding it. This merged configuration incorrectly enabled Vips to scale JPEG thumbnails, producing corrupted thumbnails with horizontal lines during the .14 rollout. The issue was only resolved after the extension’s default config was removed and the change was cherry‑picked back into the release.
mitigation_principle: Use explicit configuration overrides instead of merging defaults; validate extension registration changes with automated tests; perform regression testing on image scaling after config changes; implement feature flags for extension updates; enforce code review of configuration changes; maintain a clear separation between extension defaults and core settings

original_source: Elasticsearch cluster in eqiad lost connectivity during network maintenance, causing search outages and delayed recovery.
failure_pattern: During planned network maintenance, connectivity between Elasticsearch nodes in eqiad was severed, causing 17 nodes to leave the cluster and shards to become unavailable. The cluster stopped responding to search requests for about 10 minutes until traffic was switched to the codfw cluster and shards recovered, a process delayed by slow traffic switching and insufficient fault detection.
mitigation_principle: Increase fault detection timeouts and retries; preemptively switch traffic away from a datacenter during maintenance; simplify traffic switching procedures; centralize cluster state monitoring to reduce noisy alerts

original_source: Tool Labs proxy downtime due to insufficient nginx worker_connections
symptoms: internet access to web services disrupted
failure_pattern: The nginx worker_connections limit was set too low, causing connection errors when the proxy received more concurrent connections than allowed. This led to the proxy failing to serve requests, resulting in a brief outage of all web services accessible via the proxy.
mitigation_principle: Increase worker_connections limit; implement monitoring and alerting for connection limits; establish automated failover for proxy services; add paging and health checks for critical services

original_source: NFS outage on labstore1001 due to accidental mount of snapshot device on scratch directory
symptoms: Puppet runs failed on all tool hosts
