failure_pattern: During network maintenance, dbproxy detected a host down and routed traffic to a replica that was incorrectly configured as writable. The replica accepted writes, causing duplicate entries and breaking replication, which led to a split-brain scenario, data loss, and service unavailability until the master was restored.
mitigation_principle: enforce read-only configuration on all replicas; monitor read-only status and alert on violations; increase haproxy failover timeout; test load balancer hosts during maintenance; document and review maintenance procedures

original_source: Packet loss in asw2-a-eqiad switch stack due to topology changes caused service degradation and increased 5xx errors
failure_pattern: Topology changes (cable move and link reconfiguration) in the asw2-a-eqiad switch stack caused packet loss, which in turn led to internal service timeouts and retries. The resulting back‑pressure manifested as a surge of 5xx and 503 errors for end users.
mitigation_principle: Document and test topology changes before deployment; use automated validation and rollback procedures; implement real‑time monitoring for packet loss and link health; maintain supported topologies; log all changes and impact; employ redundant paths and avoid cable moves without verification

original_source: Multiple issues and rollbacks during the 2018-08-21 1.32.0-wmf.18 train deployment
symptoms: error: Unknown database 'wikidatawiki' on shard: s3
BadMethodCallException in Parser.php (call to getId() on a non-object)
jsonconfig license notice appearing on non‑tabular data pages
JavaScript minifier inserted a bad newline after a return statement
Call to getRevisionRecord() on a non‑object (boolean)
failure_pattern: A recent deployment of the 1.32.0‑wmf.18 train introduced a regression in the MediaWiki codebase and its deployment scripts. The faulty JavaScript minifier and changes to parser callbacks caused runtime errors and database connectivity failures, which manifested as visible errors on mediawiki.org and broken page rendering. The errors triggered automated rollback procedures, leading to multiple rollbacks and incomplete deployment of the new version.
mitigation_principle: implement automated regression tests; enforce rigorous code reviews; use feature flags for incremental rollouts; monitor application error logs in real time; establish clear rollback procedures and validate post‑deployment health checks

original_source: Issues during deployment of 1.32-wmf.22 including slow Special:Contributions, PHP notices, OAuth error, ORES timeouts, and scap canary misconfiguration.
symptoms: web request timeouts due to scap canary checks
failure_pattern: Enabling a new actor storage feature flag for a small set of wikis triggered a refactoring that slowed database access, causing Special:Contributions to become sluggish. Simultaneously, scap was configured to check canaries in a dormant datacenter due to a hardcoded list, leading to repeated 60‑second timeouts and cascading errors in ORES and OAuth components.
mitigation_principle: automated rollback for feature flags; keep canary host lists in configuration management; validate code changes with unit tests; enforce timeout settings; monitor PHP notices; use automated canary checks to detect misconfigurations

original_source: MediaWiki maintenance script caused database replication lag due to missing waitForReplication call
failure_pattern: The maintenance script updated over a million rows without invoking waitForReplication, causing slave replication lag. The lag triggered read‑only mode and slowed queries on Commons and German Wikipedia, leading to noticeable performance degradation for users.
mitigation_principle: Include waitForReplication calls in all maintenance scripts; register long‑running maintenance on the Deployments page; add dry‑run options to scripts; implement DB layer detection for large write bursts; communicate maintenance schedules clearly to sysadmins

original_source: Maps overloaded actinium web proxy with errors by trying to connect to eventbus through it.
failure_pattern: A misconfiguration caused Maps to route all traffic, including event bus messages, through the url-downloader proxy. During initial tile generation, the high volume of tile invalidation messages overloaded the proxy, producing errors that cascaded to dependent services such as restbase and citoid.
mitigation_principle: remove unnecessary proxy configuration from services; validate proxy load before deployment; disable tile invalidation during initial tile generation; audit internal IP usage and disallow internal IPs in proxy config; implement load monitoring and alerting for proxy usage

original_source: eqsin PoP outage due to power feed failures and process lapses during facility maintenance
failure_pattern: Scheduled facility maintenance caused a loss of power feed A, leading to the PoP being depooled and losing connectivity. Subsequent loss of power feed B during the same maintenance window caused a complete outage for the PoP, affecting users in the APAC region. The lack of monitoring and redundancy for the power feeds allowed the failure to propagate to the network equipment, resulting in a prolonged service disruption.
mitigation_principle: implement redundant power feeds and PDUs; monitor power feed status; require health‑checks before repooling; automate triage of maintenance alerts; add monitoring for PDUs; enforce process for facility maintenance notifications; ensure network equipment redundancy

original_source: Replication gap in wikidatawiki database due to GTID enablement and schema change during DC switchover
component: MySQL replication slave (s8 eqiad master db1071)
failure_pattern: During the DC switchover, a schema change was applied while replication was paused on the s8 eqiad master. GTID was enabled on the slave after the pause, but the slave’s GTID position was set to a later binlog position, causing it to skip 50 minutes of events. Consequently, all writes from the active DC were never replicated, leading to a replication gap and data inconsistency.
mitigation_principle: Enable GTID before applying schema changes; avoid enabling GTID on a paused slave; perform automated consistency checks across DCs; document and test replication state changes during maintenance; implement automated table checksum comparison between replicas and DCs

original_source: ParserCache hosts in eqiad lacked MySQL replication from codfw during failover, causing cache to be empty or outdated and leading to severe service degradation.
symptoms: cache empty leading to low hit ratio
failure_pattern: During the datacenter failover, replication from codfw to eqiad was not enabled for ParserCache, so new cache keys were never replicated and old keys were not purged. The result was an empty or stale cache, causing a dramatic drop in hit ratio, which in turn triggered MCS timeouts, 503 spikes, memcached errors, high CPU usage, queued requests, and sporadic 500 errors.
mitigation_principle: enable replication during failover; add replication enablement to the failover checklist; create replication alerts; monitor cache hit ratio; automate replication status verification

original_source: WDQS updater failure due to Kafka date format change from MediaWiki update
failure_pattern: A MediaWiki update changed the date format in Kafka events, causing the WDQS updater to throw a DateTimeParseException and crash. The resulting log congestion triggered systemd to restart the updater every few seconds, which overwhelmed the servers and caused SSH timeouts. Rebooting the nodes and applying a patch to use the recentchanges API eventually restored normal operation.
mitigation_principle: communicate breaking changes before deployment; make components tolerant to format changes; improve monitoring and alerting for updater failures; implement graceful failure and backoff in systemd; separate routine logging from system logs; define clear data format contracts and notify changes

original_source: Six blockers closed and one opened after train deployment with no major outages.
failure_pattern: During the train deployment, a misconfiguration in the deployment pipeline caused several blockers to appear, delaying Group1 until Thursday and Group2 until late Thursday evening. The blockers prevented the deployment from proceeding but did not affect the running services, resulting in no outages. The issue was resolved by closing six blockers and opening one, after which the train concluded without major impact.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated pre-deployment validation; improve pipeline configuration management; add monitoring for blockers; enforce rollback procedures; conduct post-mortem reviews

original_source: Tilerator service failure on maps100[1-3] due to connection refusals on November 6, 2018
root_cause_category: process crash due to lock contention
failure_pattern: The Tilerator service on maps100[1-3] crashed or failed to start, causing connection refusals on port 6534. Icinga detected the failures at 00:18 UTC, and the service was manually restarted at 07:25 UTC, restoring connectivity. The underlying issue likely stemmed from lock contention within the service, leading to process termination.
mitigation_principle: Implement non‑paging alerts for persistent failures; add runbooks for service recovery; monitor and mitigate lock contention; add health checks and automated restarts; increase redundancy and load balancing

original_source: TwoColConflict extension bug caused users with Beta feature enabled to encounter core's edit conflict interface during preview or diff.
symptoms: edit conflict interface displayed during preview or diff
failure_pattern: The TwoColConflict extension’s hook handler incorrectly triggered MediaWiki core’s edit‑conflict resolution during preview or diff for users with the Beta feature enabled. Because core’s preview/diff logic was not covered by PHPUnit or browser tests, the regression went unnoticed until the extension was deployed, and the lack of CI integration with core’s browser tests allowed the bug to reach production.
mitigation_principle: implement comprehensive integration tests covering core preview/diff flows; run core browser tests in extension CI with Beta enabled; add dedicated preview/diff test cases; enforce test coverage thresholds; enable feature‑flag testing in CI; add automated regression detection for UI changes

original_source: ores.wikimedia.org was sending 500 for all score requests for 3 hours starting from 6AM UTC due to config changes during celery version upgrade from three to two, which changed its task serializer.
symptoms: HTTP 500 errors for all score requests
failure_pattern: A puppet change merged that updated the ORES configuration to use a different Celery version, which changed the task serializer. When logrotate restarted the uwsgi services, they loaded the new config and attempted to process tasks with the wrong serializer, causing all score requests to fail with HTTP 500 for three hours until the change was reverted.
mitigation_principle: Bind services to config files so changes are applied immediately; schedule service restarts during low‑traffic windows; maintain up‑to‑date contact information for staff to enable rapid response.

original_source: Toolforge Kubernetes cluster partially unavailable due to removal of floating IPs and DNS entry for k8s-master.tools.wmflabs.org
symptoms: API server unreachable via floating IP
failure_pattern: The removal of two floating IPs and the DNS entry for k8s-master.tools.wmflabs.org broke internal DNS resolution for the Kubernetes master. As a result, toolschecker could not reach the API server, causing monitoring to fail and preventing new pods from being scheduled, while existing workloads continued to run.
mitigation_principle: Document critical infrastructure components and their dependencies; enforce change approval and verification for DNS and floating IP modifications; automate configuration management for floating IPs and DNS entries; add monitoring for DNS resolution and API server reachability; maintain a single source of truth for cluster endpoints

original_source: Incident during deployment of MediaWiki 1.33.0-wmf.8 train causing multiple errors and one rollback
symptoms: MediaWiki wikis returning 500 Internal Server Error
memory limit exceeded causing page load failures
failure_pattern: The deployment of MediaWiki 1.33.0-wmf.8 introduced code changes that were incompatible with existing extensions and database schema, causing incorrect query parameters, full table scans, and memory exhaustion. These runtime errors manifested as API failures and 500 errors across wikis, leading to a rollback.
mitigation_principle: implement automated regression testing for new releases; perform database schema compatibility checks; use feature flags for incremental rollout; monitor API error rates and memory usage; establish rollback procedures

original_source: Multiple PHP errors and undefined function calls during the 2018-12-18 deployment of MediaWiki 1.33.0-wmf.9 train.
root_cause_category: deployment process failure leading to missing or corrupted code
failure_pattern: During the 2018-12-18 deployment, the new MediaWiki 1.33.0-wmf.9 code was synchronized to some wikis but the deployment process omitted or corrupted critical extension files, causing undefined function calls and missing variables. These errors manifested as PHP fatal errors and site failures, preventing users from accessing the wiki.
mitigation_principle: implement automated code integrity checks; enforce strict deployment pipelines with version verification; run automated functional tests after deployment; maintain rollback capability; ensure environment parity across groups; perform code reviews for extension changes; use continuous integration to catch missing dependencies

original_source: WDQS update process failing due to Blazegraph allocator limit on wdqs1007 and wdqs1008
failure_pattern: Blazegraph has a hard limit of 256K allocators; when the database reached this limit, it could no longer allocate memory for new literals or dictionary entries, causing all write operations to fail while reads continued to work. The limit was hit on wdqs1007 and wdqs1008 due to their large, non‑removed dictionary entries from prior workloads.
mitigation_principle: monitor allocator counts proactively; partition large namespaces into separate databases; disable raw record mode to reduce allocator usage; inline frequently used URIs to avoid separate allocations; reload databases before reaching allocator limits

original_source: Overload of Parsoid due to RESTBase bug during Mobile-Content-Service deployment causing excessive language variant transformation requests.
symptoms: high latency for language variant transformations
root_cause_category: software bug in RESTBase content versioning logic
failure_pattern: A bug in RESTBase’s content type checking caused it to request re‑rendering of all page summaries, forwarding Accept‑Language headers to Parsoid. The resulting surge in language‑variant transformation requests overloaded Parsoid, making it unresponsive and causing timeouts for page previews.
mitigation_principle: do not forward Accept‑Language during content upgrades; add rate limiting and monitoring for language‑variant requests; perform stress testing of Parsoid HTTP API; instrument language‑variant conversion metrics; update deployment procedures to monitor logs

original_source: Outage on kartotherian service due to Cassandra replicator factor increase after maps server upgrade
root_cause_category: configuration corruption during replication factor change
failure_pattern: Increasing the Cassandra replication factor for the system_auth keyspace during the maps server upgrade triggered a reset of user permissions, causing authentication failures for the kartotherian service. The resulting authentication failures manifested as HTTP and socket timeouts, leading to a service outage until permissions were restored and traffic was rerouted.
mitigation_principle: Follow safe procedure when increasing replication factor, including recreating user permissions immediately; document best practices for system_auth replication factor changes; implement automated validation of permissions after changes; add monitoring for authentication failures

original_source: Logstash overload caused by MediaWiki log influx due to single database host failure
root_cause_category: cascading failure due to single database host outage
failure_pattern: When db1114 went down, MediaWiki generated an exceptional influx of log entries that overwhelmed the logstash ingestion pipeline. The overload caused UDP packet loss, leading to loss of logs for applications using UDP and a slowdown for those using the new logging pipeline.
mitigation_principle: Implement graceful degradation to prevent log spam when dependencies fail; add rate limiting and spam filtering to the logging pipeline; improve monitoring and capacity planning for log ingestion

original_source: Varnish upload cache misconfiguration caused 301 redirects due to erroneous Puppet change
root_cause_category: misconfiguration due to erroneous Puppet change
failure_pattern: An erroneous Puppet change updated the Varnish VCL, causing the upload cache to misconfigure and return 301 redirects for every request. The change was merged and deployed, leading to widespread service disruption for upload.wikimedia.org and maps.wikimedia.org until the patch was reverted and redeployed.
mitigation_principle: Automated configuration validation before deployment; enforce pre-deployment testing of VCL patches; implement early alerting for critical checks; standardize verification across clusters and data centers

original_source: PAWS service outage due to tools.db.svc.eqiad.wmflabs database capacity issues
failure_pattern: The tools.db.svc.eqiad.wmflabs database reached its capacity limit, causing connection refusals that propagated through multiple proxies and Kubernetes components, leading to the PAWS service becoming unavailable. The complex, poorly documented architecture delayed detection and response, resulting in prolonged outage.
mitigation_principle: Increase database capacity and implement auto-scaling; set up proactive alerting for capacity thresholds; improve documentation of PAWS architecture; add redundancy and failover for critical database components; conduct regular capacity planning and load testing; train staff on incident response for complex services

original_source: Hardware failures in cloudvirt1018 and cloudvirt1024 caused downtime and data corruption risks in CloudVPS projects.
root_cause_category: ignored hardware alerts leading to cascading failure
failure_pattern: The RAID controller failure in cloudvirt1024 was ignored for three days, allowing disk issues to accumulate and propagate to cloudvirt1018. The resulting RAID failure caused VM instances to become unreachable and storage corruption, leading to downtime and a risk of data loss. Manual intervention and delayed draining of the affected servers increased workload and extended the incident duration.
mitigation_principle: automated alert escalation and visibility; shared storage for VM instances; on-site spare disks for rapid replacement; automated disk health checks and recovery scripts; disable VM creation during maintenance via puppet; planned failovers for nova services; improved capacity planning documentation

original_source: PAWS service outage due to database connection overload and table corruption on tools.db.svc.eqiad.wmflabs
failure_pattern: A flood of connections from tools caused the MariaDB instance to exceed its max_connections limit, leading to timeouts and stalled queries. The sustained overload prevented connections from being released, causing internal table corruption and crashes. The resulting database unavailability cascaded to PAWS and Jupyter services, producing 504 errors and service outages.
mitigation_principle: Enforce per-user connection limits; monitor and alert on connection spikes; configure database to auto-restart or failover; review and optimize long-running queries; keep database software up-to-date; use replication for failover; perform regular table health checks; document and enforce database usage policies

original_source: IRC-based changes feed disrupted for 67 minutes after systemd-journald restart during security update.
symptoms: no changes pushed to IRC channel
failure_pattern: A restart of systemd-journald during a security update caused the ircecho service to lose its ability to send IRC messages. The monitoring system only verified that the ircecho process was running, not that it was actively transmitting, so the failure went unnoticed. Consequently, the IRC-based changes feed was unavailable for 67 minutes.
mitigation_principle: Implement functional health checks for dependent services; ensure monitoring verifies actual activity, not just process presence; coordinate service restart order during maintenance; add alerts for service inactivity

original_source: Invalid mediawiki-config deployment caused EventBus misconfiguration leading to logstash overload
failure_pattern: An invalid mediawiki-config deployment misconfigured the EventBus extension, causing a sudden spike in mediawiki error logs. The surge overwhelmed logstash’s persistent queue, which became unstable and failed to process events, resulting in UDP loss alerts and stalled log processing.
mitigation_principle: disable persistent queues during high load; create dashboards that correlate Kafka lag, log volume, and logstash metrics; apply Kafka consumer throttling via quotas; validate configuration changes across all wiki groups before deployment; implement automated tests for config changes

original_source: Proton PDF rendering service degraded due to 25x traffic spike from a bot
failure_pattern: A bot generated a 25× traffic spike on the Proton PDF rendering API, filling the request queue and exhausting memory, which caused the service to OOM and flap. The lack of per‑IP rate limiting allowed the bot to continue sending requests, prolonging the degradation until manual intervention and edge‑cache rate limiting were applied.
mitigation_principle: implement per‑IP rate limiting; migrate to autoscaling infrastructure; set queue length thresholds and alerts; create incident runbook; monitor traffic patterns

original_source: API request logging to eventgate-analytics caused timeouts and service disruptions due to Kafka produce errors and excessive logging.
failure_pattern: Enabling api-request logging to eventgate-analytics increased message volume to ~4000 msg/s, exceeding Kafka produce thresholds and triggering produce errors and 60‑second timeouts. These timeouts blocked MW API worker threads, causing 500 errors. The resulting error logs flooded Logstash, leading to lag and ElasticSearch indexing failures.
mitigation_principle: enable asynchronous produce mode for analytics events; set appropriate timeout for analytics events; avoid logging raw event data in logs; monitor Kafka produce error rates and set alerts; implement backpressure or rate limiting for high‑volume logging

original_source: ORES in CODFW stopped processing requests due to miscommunication during Redis server reboot.
failure_pattern: A miscommunication between SRE team members caused the backup Redis server to be rebooted while it was serving traffic. The reboot forced Redis to reload its databases and block connections, preventing ORES workers from retrieving scores and resulting in overload errors until the DNS was reverted and workers were restarted.
mitigation_principle: implement automated failover and health checks; enforce strict change management and communication protocols; use proper high-availability solutions for Redis; test DNS changes in staging; require confirmation before rebooting active servers

original_source: Gerrit outage due to elevated CPU consumption from disabled git gc
symptoms: slow clone and patch upload operations
CI failures due to git pull timeouts
failure_pattern: Disabling regular git gc caused packfiles to grow, increasing git operations' CPU usage. The elevated CPU load saturated Gerrit, making it unresponsive and causing Apache to return 5xx errors. This led to slow clone/patch uploads and CI failures, and eventually a full outage requiring a service restart.
mitigation_principle: Re-enable regular git gc maintenance tasks; monitor CPU usage with alerts; implement Prometheus exporter for Gerrit internals; enforce maintenance windows and documentation; add automated health checks for service responsiveness

original_source: Main namespace on Wikimedia Commons uneditable for 19 hours due to configuration error
failure_pattern: A configuration change was deployed that incorrectly altered the handling of the main namespace, causing edit attempts to be rejected and rendering the gallery namespace uneditable for 19 hours.
mitigation_principle: Implement comprehensive testing across all namespaces before deployment; enforce configuration validation and automated regression tests; establish clear ticket triage and escalation procedures; monitor edit failures in real-time; use feature flags for config changes

original_source: Data loss in Varnishkafka due to Kafka cluster instability caused by outdated client protocol from pyspark job
failure_pattern: An old pyspark job used a Kafka client protocol (0.8) that was incompatible with the Kafka brokers, forcing the brokers to convert messages and consume excessive heap memory. This caused Java OutOfMemory exceptions, leading to broker instability, replication lag, and temporary unavailability of topic partition leaders. Consequently, Varnishkafka producers experienced delivery failures and data loss.
mitigation_principle: Upgrade client libraries to supported protocol versions; enforce protocol compatibility checks before deployment; monitor broker memory usage and set alerts for OOM conditions; implement automated graceful restarts and rebalancing after broker restarts; improve alert sensitivity for producer delivery failures; document and enforce Kafka cluster SLOs

original_source: Zotero pods in codfw experience memory surge, causing service degradation for citoid and restbase.
failure_pattern: A sudden memory surge in the Zotero pods caused them to exceed their memory limits, leading to unresponsiveness. The LVS endpoint and citoid service checker detected the issue, but the pods remained unresponsive for almost an hour, resulting in degraded service for citoid and restbase.
mitigation_principle: implement memory usage alerts and auto-termination of pods exceeding thresholds; create runbooks for memory surge incidents; add unit tests to reproduce memory leak; improve monitoring and automated recovery; document Kubernetes debugging procedures

original_source: Search latency increased due to high CPU usage and disk pressure, leading to query rejections
root_cause_category: resource exhaustion due to disk pressure and CPU overload
failure_pattern: Disk space on key Elasticsearch nodes fell below 20%, triggering increased shard recoveries and a spike in CPU usage. The resulting resource contention caused search latency to rise 2‑5×, and the pool counter began rejecting queries, leading to a user‑visible outage. Restarting or shifting traffic off the overloaded nodes restored normal operation.
mitigation_principle: implement per‑node disk and CPU monitoring with automated alerts; replace aging hardware before critical thresholds are reached; enforce strict disk‑space limits and automatic shard reallocation; enable per‑node latency metrics for early detection; automate traffic shifting or node restarts during overload events

original_source: Tilerator and Kartotherian failed to restart during planned OpenSSL upgrade due to unreadable config and permission issues.
symptoms: service downtime for kartotherian and tilerator
failure_pattern: During a planned OpenSSL upgrade, a rolling restart of kartotherian and tilerator was initiated. The configuration files on the servers had incorrect permissions, rendering them unreadable by the services. Consequently, the services failed to start, leading to a 10‑minute outage of maps.wikimedia.org until the permissions were manually corrected.
mitigation_principle: test restart on a single host before cluster-wide deployment; verify file permissions and ownership before restarting services; automate permission checks as part of the deployment pipeline; include configuration validation in pre‑deployment checks

original_source: MediaWiki Kafka job encoding change causes job execution failures on group1 wikis
symptoms: job execution failures across multiple job types
high error rate from jobrunners (from 3/s to 100/s)
root_cause_category: encoding mismatch due to code change
failure_pattern: A change to how MediaWiki encodes jobs in Kafka (1.34.0-wmf1) produced malformed job descriptions that the jobrunners rejected with "Invalid title" errors, causing all queued jobs—including MassMessage—to fail and leading to a spike in error rates until the deployment was reverted.
mitigation_principle: Ensure backward-compatible changes to job encoding; add unit and integration tests for job serialization; include jobrunner health checks in deployment pipeline; set up alerts for jobrunner error rates; perform canary deployments with jobrunner monitoring

original_source: Varnish mailbox lag causing HTTP 503 errors and loss of approximately 82k queries.
root_cause_category: mailbox lag due to resource exhaustion
failure_pattern: Varnish mailbox lag on cp1083 climbed, causing HTTP 503 responses and loss of queries. The lag recovered on cp1083 but then increased on cp1085, leading to a brief outage that ended when the lag subsided.
mitigation_principle: monitor mailbox lag thresholds; set alerts for mailbox lag; auto-scale Varnish workers; implement backpressure mechanisms; enforce resource limits on Varnish processes

original_source: Prometheus servers in eqiad OOM-killed due to excessive memory consumption from large queries, triggered by loading Kafka dashboard with 90 days of history.
symptoms: SREs lost time due to misinterpretation
failure_pattern: Large Kafka dashboard queries spanning 90 days caused Prometheus to allocate memory at ~11 GB/minute, leading to out‑of‑memory kills. The abrupt restarts produced corrupted metrics and false traffic‑drop alerts, misleading SREs for 30–45 minutes.
mitigation_principle: implement query limits on Prometheus; monitor internal Prometheus metrics; alert on OOM events; review dashboard query scopes; upgrade Prometheus to a newer stable version

original_source: HTTP failures in eqiad traffic layer due to Varnish backend scalability issues
failure_pattern: The Varnish storage backend could not scale to handle long‑running requests, causing the HTC_RxStuff function to return EOF and generate HTC status -1 or HTTP format errors. These errors propagated to the traffic layer, resulting in a surge of HTTP 503 responses for users.
mitigation_principle: Implement scalable storage backend; monitor backend health and performance; automate restarts on failure; migrate to Apache Traffic Server; set resource limits and timeouts; use health checks and alerting

original_source: CI unresponsiveness and slow processing due to Zuul configuration change and merge job overload
failure_pattern: A Zuul configuration change introduced a bug that broke the gate and submit queue, causing the CI system to become unresponsive and stop voting on Gerrit patches. Subsequently, a large number of merge jobs were queued, overwhelming the merger processes and leading to slow processing of CI jobs. The lack of timely escalation and limited coverage of the CI stack exacerbated the impact.
mitigation_principle: implement automated configuration validation and rollback; establish clear escalation contacts and documentation; monitor queue size and set alerts; add redundancy to merger processes; perform load testing before deploying configuration changes

original_source: PHP7 opcache corruption triggered by scap during mediawiki config push causing widespread 500 errors
root_cause_category: opcache corruption due to race condition
failure_pattern: During a mediawiki configuration push, scap performed a sync-file that invalidated the PHP7 opcache. A race condition inside PHP7 caused the opcache to become corrupted, leading to corrupted code execution and a cascade of 500 errors across multiple app servers.
mitigation_principle: use opcache.validate_timestamps instead of scap opcache_reset; avoid partial opcache clears during deployments; implement health checks for PHP7 rendering; monitor opcache state; adopt atomic deployment procedures

original_source: Puppetmaster outage in codfw due to failed upgrade to Puppet 5 causing service disruption
symptoms: Puppet agent catalog sync failures across codfw fleet
failure_pattern: An upgrade to Puppet 5 on codfw servers installed puppet and facter packages that had incompatible dependencies, causing puppetmaster and puppetdb packages to be removed. This removed the puppetmaster service and its dependencies, leading to HTTP 404 responses and catalog sync failures across the codfw fleet.
mitigation_principle: perform dependency compatibility checks before upgrades; use package pinning or version constraints; test upgrades in staging environments; maintain rollback plan; automate package version validation; monitor service health immediately after upgrades; use feature flags or staged rollout; ensure proper logging of package changes

original_source: Deployment of faulty code to RESTBase nodes caused empty responses for some requests.
root_cause_category: faulty code deployment causing corrupted data writes
failure_pattern: A new code branch was deployed to two RESTBase nodes that introduced logic to copy data from old tables to new ones; the writes to Cassandra were incorrect and produced data that could not be decoded, causing the service to return empty responses and trigger monitoring alerts. The issue was isolated by truncating the affected tables, after which normal operation resumed.
mitigation_principle: implement rigorous code review and automated testing before deployment; add automated data integrity checks and monitoring for corrupted writes; use feature flags to roll out changes gradually; ensure monitoring alerts are sent to all relevant teams; establish clear rollback procedures and table truncation safeguards; enforce email notifications for monitoring failures

original_source: NFS outage in OpenStack projects due to hardcoded Keystone endpoint during cloudcontrol1003 upgrade to Debian Stretch
symptoms: NFS access failures for OpenStack projects
failure_pattern: The nfs-exportd daemon was configured with a hardcoded Keystone endpoint pointing to cloudcontrol1003, which was undergoing an upgrade and had its Keystone service unavailable. As a result, nfs-exportd could not retrieve the project list, causing NFS exports to fail for all OpenStack projects and bringing Toolforge offline.
mitigation_principle: replace hardcoded endpoints with dynamic service discovery; add unit tests for external service interactions; validate configuration changes in a staging environment before production; monitor authentication failures and implement fallback logic; use FQDNs and service names instead of concrete hostnames

original_source: High port utilization on cr2-eqiad due to excessive media requests from AWS client with python-requests User-Agent
failure_pattern: A single AWS client using the default python‑requests User‑Agent issued a large number of media requests, saturating the outbound port xe‑3/3/3 on cr2‑eqiad and causing port utilisation to exceed 80%. The saturated port limited further outbound traffic, but the impact was confined to internal monitoring and did not affect user‑facing services.
mitigation_principle: Implement per‑IP and per‑User‑Agent rate limiting; enforce the existing User‑Agent policy; block default User‑Agents such as python‑requests, curl, and python‑urllib2; monitor port utilisation and trigger alerts; notify community before blocking legitimate traffic

original_source: Operator error during Calico IP pool management caused routing issues and paging of unused service blubberoid
root_cause_category: operator error in IP pool configuration
failure_pattern: An operator mistakenly added an overlapping IP pool (10.64.64.1/24 instead of 10.64.65.0/24), causing Calico to delete the original /24 and leave nodes without valid IP blocks. The nodes continued advertising pod /32 addresses via BGP, leading to routing anomalies and a rolling restart that increased pod start latency, which triggered a page for the unused blubberoid service.
mitigation_principle: implement validation to prevent overlapping IP pool additions; enforce idempotent deletion of IP pools; use automated tests for network configuration changes; monitor BGP advertisements for anomalies; enforce minimum pod replicas per service; use controlled rolling restarts; upgrade Calico to latest stable version

original_source: Broken config change caused outage for Wikidata and Commons on canary hosts due to high error rates detected by scap.
symptoms: Wikis not loading on canary hosts
High error rates detected by scap
failure_pattern: A broken configuration change was deployed to the canary hosts, causing MediaWiki initialization to fail with assertion errors and a spike in error rates. Scap detected the high error rate and aborted the sync, but the revert was delayed because the deployer was unaware that the canary hosts would not be fixed until the second sync, resulting in a ~10‑minute outage for wikis routed to the canary hosts.
mitigation_principle: enable scap to automatically roll back changes in MediaWiki; enforce deployment policy that code is pushed live before Gerrit patches; expand canary monitoring to include all wikis, not just enwiki; ensure configuration changes are validated on all affected wikis before deployment; document and communicate deployment procedures to all deployers

original_source: Request timeouts in kartotherian codfw due to reimage of last node maps2003 during partitioning update
failure_pattern: Reimage of the last node maps2003 removed all nodes from the codfw pool, leaving kartotherian codfw with no nodes to route traffic to. This caused request timeouts for users served from codfw for approximately six minutes.
mitigation_principle: Ensure minimum node pool size before decommissioning; implement automated health checks for node pool; use blue-green deployment for partitioning updates; add redundancy and failover; automate reimage scripts with validation; monitor node pool status continuously

original_source: WDQS public endpoint in eqiad overloaded by bot traffic, leading to temporary unavailability and user agent ban.
root_cause_category: traffic overload due to bot activity
failure_pattern: A bot generated excessive traffic to the public WDQS endpoint, causing load to exceed the service’s capacity. The load balancer and backend could not handle the surge, resulting in the endpoint becoming unavailable for user queries. The existing throttling mechanisms were insufficient, so the system temporarily banned the python-requests user agent as a mitigation.
mitigation_principle: implement aggressive throttling of generic user agents; improve bot detection and rate limiting; enforce user agent policy; monitor traffic patterns; adjust load balancer thresholds; reduce log verbosity; update client user agents

original_source: AQS service outage due to Druid broker failure after data drop triggered by systemd timer fix
symptoms: 503 Service Unavailable errors on AQS edit APIs
degraded performance of Wikistats V2 website
failure_pattern: A misconfigured systemd timer caused an unintended data drop in Druid, which triggered a known Druid broker bug that locked the brokers. The locked brokers stopped serving queries, causing the AQS service to return 503 errors for edit APIs and degrading the Wikistats V2 website.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated checks before running destructive scripts; restrict destructive operations to staffed periods; document and test failure scenarios; use diagnostic tools like jstack before restarting services; enforce configuration management consistency

original_source: Jobs stopped being processed after rollout of MediaWiki 1.34.0-wmf.10 due to missing page_title property check in job executor
symptoms: Jobs not processed for group0 and group1 wikis
root_cause_category: missing required field in job specification
failure_pattern: The removal of the page_title property from the job JSON schema caused the internal job executor endpoint to reject jobs with a 400 error. Change‑Prop ignored these 400 responses and did not log the failure, so jobs were silently dropped. This led to a 12‑hour outage for group0 and group1 wikis and caused jobs that span all wikis to become stuck.
mitigation_principle: Validate required fields before processing; ensure endpoints report errors to upstream services; add logging for early validation failures; implement automated integration tests for job queue; improve observability and monitoring for job queue

original_source: WDQS public endpoint in eqiad overloaded, causing HTTP 5xx errors for  1.5 hours
root_cause_category: traffic overload due to insufficient throttling
failure_pattern: The public endpoint was overloaded by a surge of read traffic from a generic user agent (GuzzleHttp), which exceeded the throttling limits and caused the load balancer to time out and return HTTP 5xx responses. The overload cascaded to the backend Blazegraph instance, leading to a JVM thread out of control and a temporary shutdown of the updater service, resulting in a 1.5‑hour outage.
mitigation_principle: Implement stricter throttling for generic user agents; rate limit update traffic; monitor load balancer health metrics; add circuit breaker to backend services; perform capacity planning and auto‑scaling; enforce request quotas

original_source: Two unrelated incidents affecting EventStreams on the same day: Kafka broker migration issues and Varnish connection pool exhaustion due to a single IP consuming all connections.
symptoms: service health checks in UNKNOWN state
failure_pattern: During a Kafka broker migration, the EventStreams service was not updated with the new broker list, causing its daemons to lose connectivity and health checks to enter UNKNOWN state. Simultaneously, a single client IP saturated the Varnish connection pool, exhausting available connections and resulting in HTTP 502 errors for other clients.
mitigation_principle: implement per-client connection limits; ensure configuration changes propagate to dependent services; improve alerting to include broader audience and detect UNKNOWN states; document and test migration plans

original_source: Elasticsearch type error caused Logstash to reject messages, leading to Kafka backlog and loss of Mediawiki log visibility
failure_pattern: A type collision in the Elasticsearch mapping for the 'error' field caused Logstash to reject all messages from cpjobqueue and changeprop. The rejected messages accumulated in Kafka, creating a large backlog that prevented Logstash from consuming new logs, which in turn delayed visibility of Mediawiki errors for several hours.
mitigation_principle: implement schema validation and versioning for Elasticsearch mappings; add automated alerts for log ingestion failures; monitor Kafka consumer lag; enable dead‑letter queue for Logstash; enforce schema compatibility checks before deployment

original_source: Maps service outage due to cluster overload during OSM data reload
failure_pattern: During an OSM data reload, a restart of the kartotherian service on the maps eqiad cluster caused a sudden spike in CPU and request load. The cluster became overloaded, leading to timeouts and a high error rate for map tile requests. Depooling the codfw cluster and redirecting traffic allowed the eqiad cluster to recover.
mitigation_principle: perform load testing before data reload; implement graceful scaling and canary reloads; monitor cluster load thresholds and auto‑scale; enforce circuit breakers; schedule maintenance during low traffic periods; automate depooling decisions

original_source: Network fiber damage during datacenter maintenance caused memcached latency and logstash overload
failure_pattern: During routine datacenter maintenance a fiber cable between racks A6 and A7 in the virtual chassis was damaged, creating a high bit‑error rate that caused packet loss and TCP retransmits. The resulting memcached failures forced mcrouter to mark multiple shards as down, degrading application performance and producing a surge of error logs that overwhelmed Logstash. The cascading effect led to HTTP 5xx errors and noticeable latency spikes for users.
mitigation_principle: implement automated fiber health monitoring and alerts; add redundancy and failover for memcached shards; enhance log ingestion resilience with back‑pressure and message filtering; establish clear maintenance procedures and pre‑checks; improve network observability for VCP port statistics

original_source: API appserver cluster overwhelmed by expensive parsoid-batch calls causing brownouts and reduced frontend availability.
symptoms: high CPU load on API appservers
root_cause_category: resource exhaustion due to unbounded parallelism
failure_pattern: External parsoid-batch requests were not rate‑limited, causing unbounded parallelism that saturated the API appserver cluster’s CPU and memory. The resulting high CPU load triggered alerts and low HTTP availability, leading to brownouts and reduced frontend availability for API users.
mitigation_principle: Limit external request concurrency and parallelism; implement rate limiting for external API calls; add backpressure and timeout handling to prevent retries from multiplying load; aggregate request type metrics across the cluster; improve alerting to reduce noise

original_source: Database misconfiguration in Wikidata TermStore causes 500 errors on cawiki due to incorrect database name usage
symptoms: 500 internal server errors on cawiki pages
failure_pattern: The DatabaseTermIdsResolver was configured to use the wrong database name (cawiki instead of wikidatawiki), causing it to attempt connections to the wrong database on s8 replicas. This misconnection led to database connection failures, which manifested as 500 errors on cawiki pages and impacted other wikis that rely on Wikidata data.
mitigation_principle: implement validation of database configuration before deployment; use automated tests to verify database connections; enforce code review for configuration changes; add monitoring for database connection errors; maintain documentation of database interactions

original_source: Logstash outage due to failed consumer affecting operational monitoring and developer workflows for 30 minutes
symptoms: developer inability to use debugging tools
deployment failures for MediaWiki and other services
failure_pattern: The Kafka consumer in Logstash crashed, causing it to stop ingesting logs from MediaWiki servers. This halted log forwarding to downstream monitoring systems, leaving operators blind and preventing developers from using debugging tools or deploying code. The issue persisted until the consumer was manually restarted.
mitigation_principle: implement automatic restart of failed consumers; add health checks and self‑healing mechanisms; monitor consumer lag and alert proactively; add redundancy to consumer instances; improve alerting for consumer failures

original_source: Provider outage on primary transport link between eqiad and codfw causing network flapping and elevated 5xx errors
failure_pattern: A provider outage on the primary transport link between eqiad and codfw caused the link to flap, leading to routing churn and packet loss. The intermittent connectivity made backends unreachable, resulting in elevated 5xx errors and various monitoring failures.
mitigation_principle: enable automatic failover and document procedures; configure interface damping and OSPF link protection; implement robust link monitoring with Prometheus blackbox exporter; ensure alerting for link flapping

original_source: Kubernetes API server failure due to CA certificate mismatch with etcd servers caused extended Toolforge outage
symptoms: Toolforge tools cannot be launched or managed via kubectl
kube2proxy crashes and fails to watch for changes
failure_pattern: A puppet change updated the CA certificate on the etcd servers, causing the kube‑apiserver to use a different CA when connecting to etcd. The mismatched certificates prevented the API server from authenticating to etcd, causing it to fail to start and become unresponsive. This cascaded to kube2proxy and all Kubernetes webservices, making the entire Toolforge cluster appear down.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated certificate validation and versioning; enforce single source of truth for CA certificates; document and test etcd cluster processes; upgrade Kubernetes to improve error reporting; make kube2proxy resilient to API server failures; implement control plane high availability; audit puppet CA certificates

original_source: Map servers experienced CPU saturation due to badly formed requests from a bug in Kartotherian's HTTP error handler, causing partial unavailability for approximately 9 hours.
failure_pattern: A bug introduced in Kartotherian’s HTTP error handler caused it to fail to validate request parameters, leading to excessive CPU usage and timeouts on map servers. The resulting CPU saturation degraded map service availability for roughly nine hours.
mitigation_principle: implement comprehensive input validation; add unit and integration tests for request handling; perform thorough code reviews for critical components; monitor CPU usage and set alerts for abnormal spikes; establish incident response playbooks

original_source: Partial failures in citoid and cxserver services due to misconfigured Calico policy controller during CoreDNS rollout
failure_pattern: A misconfigured Calico policy controller referenced the wrong datacenter, causing network policy rules to be incorrectly applied in eqiad. original_source: Connectivity loss in rack D2 and row D due to top of rack switch failure
failure_pattern: The top‑of‑rack switch asw2‑d2‑eqiad failed, causing all hosts in rack D2 and the row D virtual‑chassis master to lose connectivity. original_source: s3 primary database master crash due to RAID backup battery failure
failure_pattern: The RAID backup battery (BBU) failed, causing the RAID controller to lose power and the host to crash. The crash rendered the MySQL master unavailable, preventing write operations and causing all s3 wikis to switch to read‑only mode while replicas remained available.

original_source: Outage during WMCS OpenStack control plane upgrade caused incorrect VM outbound IP, breaking DNS, LDAP, and NFS services
failure_pattern: During the OpenStack control plane upgrade, the Neutron SDN controller misconfigured the outbound IP address for VMs, causing traffic to appear from an unexpected source. original_source: Equinix Singapore IXP peer flap caused routing daemon overload and service outage in eqsin PoP
root_cause_category: routing daemon overload due to excessive BGP/OSPF flapping
failure_pattern: An Equinix Singapore IXP peer flapped heavily, causing the routing daemon on cr1-eqsin to become overloaded. The overload forced all BGP and OSPF sessions to flap or go down, which in turn broke connectivity to the main datacenters and caused local caches to return 500 errors to users.

original_source: Wikidata API timeouts due to increased database read load from backported Wikibase changes reducing deadlocks
symptoms: high API response times for writes
failure_pattern: Backported Wikibase changes that stopped locking and used DISTINCT caused a spike in read traffic on database slaves during term migration. original_source: Roll out of wmf.8 to group1 caused outage due to database errors and rollback issues.
failure_pattern: The rollout of wmf.8 to group1 introduced configuration changes that caused a spike in database errors in logstash, triggering Icinga alerts and degrading performance of group1 and group2 wikis. mitigation_principle: implement automated database health checks before deployment; use canary deployments with rollback safeguards; monitor database error rates and set alert thresholds; separate application and database concerns; enforce rollback procedures; add circuit breakers; use feature flags; perform staged rollouts; add alerting thresholds

original_source: Cite extension bug caused PHP notice logspam and missing references due to shallow cloning of parser state
root_cause_category: shallow cloning of parser state causing shared mutable state
failure_pattern: The Message class requests its own Parser via PHP's clone, which shallowly copies the Cite extension’s state. The shared state array is cleared by a fresh Message parser, wiping out previously stored references. This results in a flood of PHP notice logspam and missing references in rendered pages.
mitigation_principle: avoid shallow cloning of objects with mutable state; use deep copy or custom clone methods; add unit and integration tests for cloning behavior; enforce immutability of shared state; review code for dynamic properties; implement defensive copying; add static analysis for clone usage

original_source: Commons wiki database replicas lagged due to incorrect SQL query causing stale results and incorrect category counts.
root_cause_category: incorrect SQL query syntax leading to unintended bulk updates
failure_pattern: An UPDATE statement in WikiPage::updateCategoryCounts omitted quotes around the category ID, causing MySQL to treat the numeric literal as a pattern and update all categories whose titles begin with "11". The large, unindexed update saturated the primary replica, delaying replication to secondary replicas and producing stale reads and incorrect category counts for users.
mitigation_principle: enable strict SQL mode to catch unquoted identifiers; add unit tests for critical database update queries; implement query linting and review for schema changes; set replication lag alerts with lower thresholds; use LIMIT 1 for single-row updates; enforce code review for all database schema modifications

original_source: Job queue backlog caused by image annotation jobs with release timestamps in Kafka Job Queue
failure_pattern: The MachineVision extension enqueued image annotation jobs with a 48‑hour release timestamp, a feature that the Kafka job queue interprets as a blocking wait. These blocking waits saturated the queue, creating a backlog that slowed or stalled all other job types. As a result, a wide range of user‑facing tasks experienced severe delays.
mitigation_principle: implement feature compatibility checks; add monitoring for job backlog spikes; document unsupported features; improve queue handling of unknown job types

original_source: Accidental blocking of all enwiki search API traffic due to erroneous VCL configuration change
symptoms: HTTP 403 errors for search API requests
search API unavailable for bots and mobile app users
failure_pattern: An incorrect VCL configuration change intended to block a specific bot was merged and deployed via Puppet, but the rule was too broad and applied to all search API traffic. This caused Varnish to return HTTP 403 for every request to /w/api.php with srsearch, resulting in widespread API unavailability for bots and mobile app users.
mitigation_principle: Implement thorough code review for VCL changes; expand automated Varnish tests to cover all traffic patterns; introduce structured traffic blocking rule abstraction; add monitoring for API error rates; ensure on-call coverage during holidays; enable quick rollback mechanisms

original_source: MediaWiki configuration change causing EventBus TLS timeout led to widespread service outages and Varnish frontend crashes
failure_pattern: The change to enable TLS for EventBus caused PHP7 rendering timeouts on MediaWiki application servers, which in turn overwhelmed the Varnish frontends, leading to memory allocation failures and crashes. The resulting loss of backend availability was compounded by ATS‑tls misidentifying the crashed Varnish instances as down, causing a cascading outage across the service.
mitigation_principle: require code review for configuration changes; enforce canary deployments with extended monitoring; prevent automatic php‑fpm restarts during deployments; make Varnish frontend resilient to memory allocation failures; raise alert severity for Varnish crashes; ensure ATS‑tls immediately marks Varnish up after restart; use per‑cgroup CPU graphs for rapid diagnostics

original_source: Service degradation due to traffic surge following Kobe Bryant's death announcement causing high contention and memcached saturation.
failure_pattern: The sudden surge in edits and page views caused an editing stampede that saturated the network link of two memcached servers, making about 1/9th of the keys unavailable. This cache unavailability triggered a spike in cache misses for Babel calls, flooding the API and appserver clusters with high latency requests and CPU contention, ultimately rendering the MediaWiki application layer largely unavailable.
mitigation_principle: implement rate limiting for high‑traffic events; add local memcached instances to reduce network load; monitor memcached key availability and latency; add circuit breakers for cache failures; pre‑emptively scale caching layer during high traffic; use aggressive timeouts for external calls

original_source: External demand for expensive MediaWiki API query caused slowdown and timeouts, affecting Recommendation API service availability.
symptoms: partial unavailability of Recommendation API service

failure_pattern: An external client issued an expensive MediaWiki API query that consumed significant server resources, causing the MediaWiki API web servers to become slower overall. original_source: Babel extension cache miss spike caused increased API load and appserver latency due to self-calls over HTTPS

failure_pattern: The Babel extension attempted to retrieve language data from WANObjectCache; a cache miss triggered a self‑call over HTTPS to the API server, adding TLS overhead and increasing API load. The resulting CPU spike on appservers caused higher latency and timeouts, which in turn produced more cache misses, creating a feedback loop that degraded overall performance until the cache hit ratio recovered.

original_source: Maps servers fully saturated on CPU, resulting in increased latency and errors, mitigated by blocking non-Wikimedia traffic.
root_cause_category: resource exhaustion due to traffic overload
failure_pattern: The Maps servers were already near capacity; a Mediawiki API outage caused a surge in requests to the Maps backend, driving CPU usage to 100% and causing health checks to fail. This led to a cascade of 503/504 errors and the blocking of external traffic, which was incorrectly applied to all requests, further degrading service until capacity was rebalanced and the block was corrected.
mitigation_principle: implement capacity monitoring and auto‑scaling; segregate external traffic with rate limiting; improve monitoring visibility for Kartotherian; perform capacity planning and load testing; establish clear traffic routing policies; ensure proper code review for CDN cache miss rules; maintain SRE staffing and expertise

original_source: Widespread service timeouts after deploying MediaWiki 1.35.0-wmf.18 to group2 wikis due to a configuration typo in Wikibase.
failure_pattern: A typo in the Wikibase configuration prevented the new store setting from taking effect, so client wikis continued to read from the old store while the extension default had switched to the new store. original_source: API and application server unresponsiveness due to aggressive bot scraping on zhwiki with expensive template parsing
root_cause_category: resource exhaustion from uncached expensive template parsing
failure_pattern: The bot made a large number of parse requests that bypassed the parser cache, forcing the API server to perform expensive template parsing for each request. original_source: Outage caused by configuration typo in Wikibase client settings during deployment
failure_pattern: A typo in the Wikibase client configuration caused the deployment to use the default setting, which switched group2 wikis to read from the new term store for items up to 8 million. original_source: CDN edge cache depooling during maintenance caused 15-minute outage in eqiad
root_cause_category: maintenance-triggered cascading failure due to insufficient safeguards
failure_pattern: During maintenance, operators depooled all caching servers without repooling them, and the tooling allowed unlimited depooling. Because the system had no safeguards, the entire eqiad cache layer was taken offline. This caused all traffic routed to eqiad to be dropped, leading to widespread service outages for users.

original_source: Router hardware failure in esams caused widespread service disruption due to coinciding hardware failures and single point of failure concerns.

original_source: Logged-out users saw interface in browser language due to unset wgULSLanguageDetection from configuration change

original_source: Parsercache database overload due to malfunctioning host causing increased latency and connection spikes

original_source: Unexpected loss of internal connectivity to codfw hosts due to linecard restart during maintenance exposing network design flaw

original_source: Data loss in Wikidata's wb_items_per_site table due to misconfigured cron script executing update.php path
symptoms: database query errors on page loads
high 50X error rate to cache servers

failure_pattern: A weekly cron job executed a misconfigured script that bypassed production checks and ran LoadExtensionSchemaUpdates, which dropped the wb_items_per_site table. original_source: Virtual chassis link failure between asw2-d1-eqiad and asw2-d8-eqiad causing packet loss and MediaWiki exceptions

original_source: Wikidata Query Service outage on May 5th, 2020 due to failed deployment caused by incorrect procedure and code bug removing serialVersionUID from WKTSerializer class.

original_source: Thumbor service disruption due to excessive requests from external client causing 503 errors and latency spikes

uploaded images not visible on Wikipedia
race condition causing missing file entries

original_source: Logstash indexes were temporarily stale due to newer messages from Kafka not being processed.

original_source: Lilypond seemingly bypassing security restrictions.

original_source: Primary hard drive crash on Singapore POP router cr3-eqsin caused brief traffic loss

original_source: HTTPS redirect changes caused timeouts for Termbox and Wikifeeds due to blocked egress traffic from Kubernetes clusters.

original_source: Stored XSS security issue in MobileFrontend talk pages patched the same day

original_source: Power cable issue during PDU upgrade caused network switch to reboot with incorrect firmware, leading to host unavailability and service disruptions.

original_source: Faulty configuration deployed for mobileapps caused broken CSS and JS links in mobile-html content during reconfiguration of services to use service proxy middleware.

original_source: Replication stopped on s5 database replicas due to duplicate key in ipblocks table, causing watchlist and recentchanges delays.

original_source: Sensitive credentials leaked via publicly accessible memcached servers without authentication.

original_source: Slow loading of French Wikipedia main page due to oversized FeaturedFeeds cache entries

original_source: High CPU and socket timeout errors on jobrunners due to 4K video uploads causing job backlog and server unavailability.

failure_pattern: Large 4K video uploads from a fast internal connection triggered many downscale jobs on the jobrunners, causing excessive CPU usage and socket timeouts. The resulting overload created a backlog in the job queue and made several mw-related servers unavailable.

original_source: Mailman2 attachments publicly accessible due to lack of archiving controls and public URLs

original_source: Network switch failure causes partial rack outage in Codfw cluster affecting multiple services
failure_pattern: A faulty network switch caused loss of connectivity for eight hosts in a rack, which in turn made several service nodes (Elasticsearch, Swift, Edge cache, DNS) unreachable. original_source: Increased latency and errors on commons.wikimedia.org due to bot-induced load on databases and API webservers
failure_pattern: A bot generated excessive traffic that overloaded the commonswiki databases and API webservers, exhausting resources and causing cache misses and authentication failures. original_source: Instability serving wiki uncached content due to overload from bot requests on commonswiki

failure_pattern: Excessive bot traffic to commonswiki saturated the API and database servers, creating resource contention that propagated to other wikis. original_source: Network stack crash on ms-be1062 caused Swift timeouts and Thumbor cluster resource starvation during Swift rebalance.
failure_pattern: A kernel bug caused the network stack on ms‑be1062 to crash, blackholing all traffic to that node. original_source: Wikimedia Commons outage due to InnoDB contention on primary database s4, triggered by high query load from GlobalUsage extension.

failure_pattern: A surge of long‑running queries from the GlobalUsage extension overloaded the InnoDB engine on the primary s4 master, causing threadpool blocking and replication errors. original_source: Data loss in revision text cache due to bug in mediawiki-BagOStuff refactor causing increased database load and HTTP 5xx errors

failure_pattern: A refactor of mediawiki-BagOStuff caused the SqlBlobStore to fail to recognize Memcached as an eligible caching layer, resulting in a dramatic increase in cache misses. original_source: Connectivity issues to Eqsin cluster in Singapore caused wikis to be largely unreachable from Asia for 35 minutes.

original_source: Traffic surge in Ulsfo cluster caused network port capacity issues affecting San Francisco DC regions.

original_source: MediaWiki API request failures due to EventGate deployment issue in codfw

original_source: Network switch failure in codfw rack A2 caused service outages and failover issues

failure_pattern: The unresponsive network switch handling rack A2 traffic caused all hosts in that rack to become unreachable. original_source: Outage caused by slow DynamicPageList queries from Russian Wikinews overloading database cluster
failure_pattern: The creation of a new category linked to ~180,000 pages triggered many DynamicPageList queries. original_source: Parsoid parse2007 server failure due to PHP-opcache corruption causing 9-hour outage in page parsing and saving

high error rate visible in Grafana

original_source: Increased database load caused slow backend responses and request failures for 37 minutes.

original_source: Table of Contents language conversion failure and rollback-induced disappearance across Wikimedia wikis due to inadequate testing and communication

original_source: Data loss in CirrusSearch commonsfile index due to developer's high-volume queries and index recreation

original_source: BGP routing error caused 12-minute connectivity loss between Eqiad and remote data centers via public IPs

original_source: Outgoing email delays due to kernel bug affecting iptables conntrack on mail server mx2001

original_source: MediaWiki availability on all wikis for logged-in users and uncached content disrupted due to database repooling and network load on db1099 in s8 section
