The throttled pods could not process messages quickly enough, creating a backlog that starved the api_appserver of idle PHP‑FPM workers and degraded request latency.
mitigation_principle: Implement per‑pod CPU limits and monitoring; enable autoscaling based on queue depth; validate logging level changes in staging before production; add alert correlation to detect upstream bottlenecks; perform load testing for major deployments

original_source: WDQS outage in codfw due to excessive thread pool usage triggering Blazegraph deadlock
failure_pattern: A sudden influx of requests overloaded the thread pool of the Blazegraph backend in codfw, causing CPU load and throttling filter state to grow. This triggered a known bug where improper thread management leads to a deadlock, blocking all query processing. The deadlock caused the service to become unresponsive, leading to query failures and timeouts for users.
mitigation_principle: Implement thread pool limits and backpressure; add circuit breaker to prevent deadlocks; monitor thread pool usage and CPU load; apply application-level throttling; patch or upgrade Blazegraph to fix deadlock bug

original_source: A wrong configuration change caused sessionstore pods to be unschedulable in our WikiKube cluster, resulting in failed edits across all projects for 9 minutes.
failure_pattern: A manual removal of nodeAffinity for specific rack rows from the sessionstore deployment caused the pods to become unschedulable in the WikiKube cluster. Without running pods, the sessionstore service could not respond to edit requests, leading to a 9‑minute outage for all users.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated configuration validation; enforce code review for k8s deployment changes; use declarative configuration management; add pre‑deployment tests for pod schedulability; monitor pod scheduling status

original_source: API overload and outage during 2022 World Cup final due to DiscussionTools extension and traffic spike
root_cause_category: resource exhaustion due to excessive API calls
failure_pattern: The DiscussionTools extension added a ResourceLoader module that triggered an API call on almost every page view, creating a surge of uncached POST requests to the API cluster. During the World Cup final, overall traffic spiked by roughly 50%, overwhelming the limited PHP‑FPM worker threads and causing 5xx errors and high latency. The overload persisted until traffic naturally fell, after which latency gradually improved.
mitigation_principle: implement request throttling or caching for high‑frequency API calls; monitor worker thread utilization and set alerts; perform load testing after deployments; document and automate restart procedures; add circuit breaker for heavy modules; use feature flags to disable problematic modules during traffic spikes; ensure proper scaling of API workers

original_source: Sudden spike in requests overloaded shellbox-syntaxhighlight service, causing slow responses and errors for 10 minutes.
failure_pattern: A sudden spike in requests to the shellbox-syntaxhighlight service overloaded the service, exceeding the capacity of its 12 replicas and causing worker saturation. The overload led to increased latency and request failures for about 10 minutes until the service was manually scaled up to 40 replicas and traffic subsided.
mitigation_principle: implement autoscaling based on request rate; monitor worker saturation metrics; set up alerts for sudden request spikes; document scaling procedures; perform load testing for burst scenarios

original_source: API errors and elevated 5xx due to database overload on db1143 from GlobalUsage queries
root_cause_category: resource exhaustion due to high query load
failure_pattern: An edit or refreshlinks event triggered onLinksUpdateComplete, which issued hundreds of GlobalUsage SELECT queries to the commons database cluster. The resulting 300 concurrent queries overloaded db1143, causing it to become unresponsive and be depooled. The sudden drop in load on db1143 caused a spike in reads on the en.wikipedia cluster, leading to API 5xx errors and suggestion failures.
mitigation_principle: implement query throttling or caching for GlobalUsage; add circuit breaker for database overload; monitor query rates per server; add rate limiting; improve alerting for database load spikes; ensure graceful degradation of services

original_source: Network outage at eqsin due to transport link failure during planned maintenance
root_cause_category: planned maintenance causing transport link failure
failure_pattern: The planned maintenance on the transport provider cut one of the two transport links to eqsin. The other link was already down due to a long fiber cut, leaving eqsin with a single operational link. The loss of connectivity caused BGP sessions to fail, leading to host outages and DNS depooling, which resulted in packet loss and user‑facing content access failures.
mitigation_principle: implement redundant transport links with automatic failover; monitor transport link health and alert on single link failure; parse maintenance notifications and alert on conflicting maintenance; depool sites promptly when connectivity degrades; maintain up‑to‑date documentation of transport links and maintenance windows

original_source: Switch asw-b2-codfw failure leading to loss of systems in B2 and reduced redundancy
failure_pattern: The asw-b2-codfw network switch failed, causing all hosts in B2 to go down and lose connectivity. The failover to the B7 switch was successful for the master, but B2 systems remained offline, leading to reduced redundancy. Because the switch could not be remotely power‑cycled, the only resolution was to replace the hardware the following business day.
mitigation_principle: Automate switch failure detection and alerting; link runbooks directly to alerts; define clear out‑of‑hours escalation procedures; enable remote power cycling or redundant power paths; regularly test and replace failing switches; document and automate recovery procedures

original_source: MediaWiki crash for logged-in users due to inconsistent code state during backport deployment
symptoms: high exception and fatal error rate in MediaWiki appserver
root_cause_category: deployment race condition between file sync and php-fpm restart
failure_pattern: During the backport deployment, extension.json was synced to the servers before the php‑fpm process was restarted. MediaWiki re‑read the new configuration while still running the old PHP code, creating an inconsistent state that caused the application to crash for all logged‑in page views. The revert left the cluster in this inconsistent state until php‑fpm restarted, prolonging the outage.
mitigation_principle: ensure atomic deployment of code and configuration files; force php‑fpm restart before applying configuration changes; add canary checks to detect runtime errors after file sync; update status page automatically on deployment; avoid cancelling deployments mid‑sync to prevent inconsistent state

original_source: Network connectivity loss in codfw row B due to Junos bugs during switch replacement prep work
failure_pattern: The prep work to bring a replacement switch online triggered a Junos bug that caused instability in row B, disrupting connectivity between switches. An operator error then triggered a second Junos bug that broke IPv6 connectivity across the entire row. The combination of these bugs resulted in all hosts in codfw row B losing network connectivity, while IPv4 remained functional.
mitigation_principle: implement automated change validation for switch replacement; use standardized cabling and configuration procedures; maintain up-to-date firmware across all switches; create visual dashboards for service routing state; plan regular switch refresh cycles

original_source: Session storage outage in eqiad due to Cassandra quorum issues after host reboot
failure_pattern: A routine reboot of Cassandra host sessionstore1001 caused the node to leave the cluster; Kask removed pooled connections and rerouted traffic to the remaining nodes. When the node rejoined, clients still used it as a coordinator, but the cluster could not achieve LOCAL_QUORUM consistency, leading to session storage errors and a 15‑minute outage for login and editing.
mitigation_principle: implement automatic alerting for elevated error rates; de‑pool datacenter before host reboots; improve connection‑pooling to handle node re‑join; monitor consistency‑level failures; add redundancy or failover for session storage

original_source: Outage caused by non-robust deployment configuration during Kartotherian rollback
failure_pattern: A new kartotherian deployment was rolled out without the required "--env" flag, causing the configuration templates to be malformed. During the rollback attempt, the service failed to restart, leading to a complete outage of the maps service and triggering spurious monitoring alerts.
mitigation_principle: implement robust deployment automation with environment validation; enforce configuration template linting in CI; containerize services; improve deployment documentation; automate monitoring configuration; use automated rollback safeguards

original_source: Data loss in mediawiki.page-undelete event stream due to accidental unregistration of hook handler
failure_pattern: A merge of a change to the EventBus extension inadvertently unregistered the EventBusHooks:onPageUndelete hook handler, causing the mediawiki.page-undelete event stream to stop emitting events. Downstream services such as WDQS and WCQS, which rely on these events to keep their data in sync, therefore missed undelete events for over three months, leading to data inconsistencies and missing pages. The issue remained undetected because no automated alerting existed for the missing stream throughput.
mitigation_principle: implement automated stream throughput alerts; enforce code review for critical configuration changes; add automated tests for event stream presence; monitor downstream consistency; maintain change impact analysis

original_source: Logstash message congestion in eqiad due to Parsoid exception flood causing 2h14m latency spike
failure_pattern: A flood of PHP notices from Parsoid caused a surge of log events that Logstash could not process quickly enough, leading to Kafka consumer lag and a backlog of messages. The backlog exceeded the latency budget, resulting in a 2h14m violation of Logstash's latency SLO.
mitigation_principle: Add rate limiting to upstream log generators; implement backpressure handling in Logstash; enable alerting and paging for Kafka consumer lag; improve monitoring dashboards; add automated throttling; review and tighten exception handling in Parsoid

original_source: Editing disruption during live switchover test due to read-only mode misconfiguration in codfw and eqiad datacenters
symptoms: editing failed for some users in codfw datacenter
desktop users redirected to edit through eqiad
root_cause_category: configuration corruption due to incorrect data type
failure_pattern: The live switchover test script set the ReadOnly flag to a string value instead of a boolean, causing the configuration management tool to interpret it as true. This propagated the read-only state to both codfw and eqiad datacenters, disabling editing for users. The misconfiguration was not detected by monitoring, leading to a prolonged outage.
mitigation_principle: Implement strict type validation for configuration values; automate idempotent read-write state setting across all datacenters; add monitoring for read-only state changes; enforce consistent behavior across mobile and desktop; use automated rollback on configuration errors

original_source: Wiki outage due to accidental depooling of ATS backends during HAProxy upgrade in esams and eqiad
failure_pattern: During a routine HAProxy upgrade, the depool operation for ATS backends was executed but the subsequent pool command was mismatched, leaving the backends out of the pool. This caused cache hosts to have no available backends, resulting in 503/500 errors for both cached and uncached traffic and a significant drop in editing activity for users in affected regions.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated validation of depool/pool operations; add pre/post-deployment checks for backend pool state; enhance alert descriptions with context; use canary deployments for HAProxy upgrades; ensure manual operations are logged to central system

original_source: PHP worker threads exhaustion due to MariaDB query killer bug on db1127 running outdated version 10.6.10
failure_pattern: An outdated MariaDB 10.6.10 instance on db1127 contained a bug where the query killer failed to terminate long‑running queries, causing the database to become overloaded and saturate connections. The resulting high DB response times and connection pressure forced PHP‑FPM workers to exhaust idle threads, leading to PHP worker thread exhaustion and degraded API performance.
mitigation_principle: Keep database software up to date; implement automated patch deployment; monitor query killer effectiveness; enforce query timeouts and connection limits; add health checks for DB saturation; maintain redundancy and failover for critical DB hosts

original_source: Data loss on GitLab production host due to restore job not being disabled during planned switchover
failure_pattern: The restore job was not disabled on the new production host during the planned switchover, causing a backup to be restored on the production host and wiping recent changes. This resulted in data loss and a brief service outage.
mitigation_principle: automate enable/disable of restore jobs based on instance status; double-check timers after failover; add safeguards to restore scripts; implement automated failover tooling; enforce configuration validation checks

original_source: Mailman outages due to runner crash during network maintenance caused two-day email delivery failure
symptoms: mail delivery failure for community mailing lists
failure_pattern: During the eqiad row A switch upgrade, network maintenance caused the mailman3 out runner process to lose connectivity to MariaDB, leading to a crash. The crash was not automatically restarted, so outgoing mail remained queued while incoming mail was still accepted. The backlog persisted for two days until the service was manually restarted, after which the queue cleared.
mitigation_principle: Add automatic restart for crashed runner processes; monitor runner process count and queue size; include affected hosts in maintenance notifications; improve alert visibility and reduce noise; ensure database connectivity monitoring; implement health checks for mailman3

original_source: Outage in eqiad LVS during scap deploy and LVS reimage caused traffic disruption for 11 minutes
failure_pattern: During a scap deploy, an LVS node was reimaged, causing that node to go down. The loss of the LVS node led to depooling of many eqiad servers, which in turn made the eqiad front‑edge unavailable for user traffic, resulting in an 11‑minute outage.
mitigation_principle: Avoid concurrent scap deploys and LVS maintenance; enforce and document scap lock; coordinate maintenance windows; implement automated checks to prevent reimage during active scap; add redundancy to LVS nodes; monitor LVS node health before depooling

original_source: Phabricator outage during GitLab maintenance due to widget error
failure_pattern: A new Phabricator widget was deployed after a GitLab host switch. During a subsequent GitLab maintenance the widget attempted to fetch data from GitLab while it was in maintenance mode, causing 502 errors and an invalid argument in the widget code. This cascade of failures prevented Phabricator tasks from loading and resulted in runtime exception messages for users.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated health checks for third‑party integrations; add unit tests for widget error handling; enforce code review and testing before deployment; deploy widget changes in a staged manner with rollback capability; monitor integration endpoints for failures

original_source: Prometheus instances down in ulsfo and eqsin due to corrupted WAL and chunks_heads after Bullseye upgrade
symptoms: Prometheus service down in ulsfo and eqsin
root_cause_category: corrupted data files due to race condition during upgrade
failure_pattern: During the Bullseye upgrade, data was synchronized and VMs rebooted; a race condition prevented the Prometheus process from shutting down cleanly, leaving WAL and chunks_heads corrupted. The corrupted files blocked Prometheus from starting, causing an 8‑hour outage and loss of observability in two data centers.
mitigation_principle: Implement graceful shutdown and verification steps before upgrades; add integrity checks for WAL and chunks_heads; enforce replica labels and fail deployment if missing; add alerts for missing data from Prometheus; update migration procedures and documentation

original_source: The rdf-streaming-updater application in CODFW became unstable and stopped sending updates, resulting in stale data for users connecting through CODFW.
root_cause_category: Flink runtime bug causing resource exhaustion
failure_pattern: A bug in Flink (FLINK-22597) caused the rdf-streaming-updater job to become unstable during a backfill, leading to CPU throttling and rapid memory growth in Kubernetes. The lack of RocksDB compaction caused the job to run out of memory and produce abnormally large checkpoints, resulting in repeated failures and stale data for users accessing WDQS from CODFW.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated alert escalation for critical services; document and automate remediation steps for switching between Kubernetes and Yarn; allocate sufficient resources for backfill jobs; monitor RocksDB compaction and checkpoint sizes; apply patches for known Flink bugs promptly

original_source: Video scaling job overloaded jobrunner server, causing flapping alerts and requiring depooling and process termination.
symptoms: increased latency for video upload processing
root_cause_category: resource exhaustion due to excessive ffmpeg processes
failure_pattern: A large video‑scaling job spawned many ffmpeg processes on server mw1469, which was both a jobrunner and a videoscaler. The CPU and memory capacity were maxed out, causing the jobrunner service to become overloaded and alerts to flake. The overload also impacted the videoscaler service, leading to flapping alerts. The incident was mitigated by depooling the server from videoscaler and killing the runaway ffmpeg processes, restoring jobrunner stability.
mitigation_principle: Isolate resource‑intensive jobs onto dedicated servers; implement capacity monitoring and automatic depooling; enforce runbook procedures for killing runaway processes; separate jobrunner and videoscaler workloads; add alert thresholds for CPU usage; use load balancing to prevent single‑node overload

original_source: External abusive queries caused 5xx errors and timeouts in WDQS service from CODFW datacenter, mitigated by requestctl rule.
root_cause_category: external abusive queries causing resource exhaustion
failure_pattern: An external user repeatedly sent an expensive query to the WDQS service in CODFW, causing the service to spend excessive time in old garbage collection and generate 5xx errors and timeouts for users. The lack of request throttling allowed the query to overwhelm the service, leading to degraded performance and eventual failure for affected users. A requestctl rule was deployed to mitigate the abuse, followed by a rolling restart to restore stability.
mitigation_principle: implement request throttling and rate limiting; add automated abuse detection and requestctl rules; monitor query cost and GC metrics; improve alert granularity for abusive patterns; enforce query cost limits; perform capacity planning for GC

original_source: LVS server downtime during scap deploy causes service outage in eqiad
failure_pattern: During a scap deployment, an LVS server (lvs1019) was taken down for maintenance while a deploy was ongoing, causing its backends to be marked down but still pooled. This led to multiple servers being depooled and the load balancer becoming unable to serve traffic, resulting in 503 errors and high latency for users.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated health checks for load balancers before maintenance; schedule maintenance to avoid overlapping with critical deployments; use redundant load balancer instances; enforce pre-deployment validation; add circuit breakers to prevent cascading failures; monitor load balancer status; maintain a maintenance window policy; use blue-green deployment for load balancers

original_source: Wikireplicas lag and data unavailability due to MariaDB replication bugs and version issues from 2023-05-25 to 2023-06-01
failure_pattern: A bug in MariaDB 10.4.29 caused replication errors that broke the slave SQL state, leading to severe replication lag and data inconsistency. The broken replication prevented replicas from receiving updates, making Wikireplicas data stale or unavailable for users and tools. Attempts to downgrade and reclone the databases were hampered by the same underlying bug and incomplete recovery procedures, prolonging the outage.
mitigation_principle: implement robust replication health monitoring and alerting; maintain version compatibility and test upgrades in staging; document and automate replica setup and recovery procedures; perform regular consistency checks and failover testing; use automated rollback on replication failure

original_source: Unintentional +2 on a config patch without deployment in mediawiki-config
failure_pattern: A configuration patch was mistakenly given a +2 vote in the mediawiki-config repository, a vote that is normally reserved for code changes. This mis-vote was applied without an accompanying deployment, creating a mismatch between the repository state and the live configuration. The error was detected within a minute and the patch was reverted, preventing any actual service disruption.
mitigation_principle: Enforce separate voting workflows for config and code repositories; add automated checks to flag +2 votes on config repos; require deployment tags for config changes; provide training on repository usage; implement peer review for config changes

original_source: Partial outage on dawiktionary, dawiki, and svwiktionary due to data migration bug involving bash double-quote interpretation
failure_pattern: A bash script used for data migration misinterpreted double‑quote characters, producing malformed data entries that were written to the database and cached in the object cache. The corrupted data caused MediaWiki to raise fatal exceptions for users browsing the affected wikis, resulting in intermittent 500 errors until the DBA corrected the migration script.
mitigation_principle: implement unit tests for migration scripts; enforce strict quoting or escape handling in scripts; perform post‑migration data integrity checks; version‑control and review all migration code; automate regression tests for data migrations; monitor cache consistency after migrations

original_source: Search broken on Wikidata and Commons due to missing text_search analyzer after Elasticsearch reindex
failure_pattern: During a routine reindex of the Wikibase indices, the text_search analyzer was removed as part of an analyzer deduplication effort. The token_count_router feature continued to reference this analyzer, so when the new index was promoted to production, all queries that used the router failed with an unknown analyzer error, causing search to break on both Wikidata and Commons.
mitigation_principle: implement automated validation of index mappings before promotion; add alerting on search failures; run representative test queries before alias switch; include analyzer existence checks in reindex scripts; use feature flags for new analyzers

original_source: Data loss in mw-page-content-change-enrich application due to oversized Kafka message causing Flink Taskmanager shutdown
failure_pattern: An oversized Kafka message exceeded the configured maximum message size, causing the Flink Taskmanager to crash and shut down. With the Taskmanager offline, the mw-page-content-change-enrich application stopped producing enriched events, leading to a service outage.
mitigation_principle: increase Kafka max message size; filter out oversized messages; implement message size validation; monitor Kafka consumer lag; set alert thresholds for message size

original_source: mw-on-k8s outage due to wrong tls cert
symptoms: service unavailability for a subset of traffic
failure_pattern: A merge of a global Kubernetes default change switched the default TLS certificate source to cert-manager. The subsequent mediawiki deployment pulled the wrong certificate for TLS termination, causing the ingress controller to present an invalid cert. Clients received TLS handshake failures and HTTP errors, leading to service outages for approximately 30 minutes.
mitigation_principle: Implement stricter CI validation for certificate changes; use canary deployments for k8s changes; add automated checks for TLS configuration before promotion; monitor ingress certificate validity; ensure fallback to default cert

original_source: Log aggregation failure on Hadoop worker nodes due to incorrect log compression type configuration.
symptoms: Airflow task failures due to missing logs
No logs found errors in Airflow alerts
YARN jobs succeed but downstream tasks fail
failure_pattern: The YARN log aggregation service was configured with the wrong compression type (gzip instead of gz), causing logs to be compressed in an unsupported format. Airflow attempted to fetch and decompress these logs, failed, and marked tasks as failed even though the underlying YARN jobs had succeeded. This misconfiguration led to widespread Airflow task failures across the cluster.
mitigation_principle: Validate configuration changes on a test cluster before production; automate service restarts after config changes; add alerts for config file modification time versus service start time; document correct compression type values; implement automated monitoring for log aggregation failures

original_source: Elasticsearch unavailable due to unexpected query routing during datacenter switchover causing increased latency and search delays
failure_pattern: During the primary datacenter switchover, RESTBase sent POST requests for cacheable "more_like" queries instead of GET, causing CirrusSearch to route those queries to the primary datacenter (codfw) rather than the non‑primary (eqiad). The resulting overload dropped cache hit rates, increased response times, and triggered PoolCounter rejections, which manifested as search delays and intermittent unavailability for end users.
mitigation_principle: Validate HTTP method for cacheable queries; enforce routing rules during datacenter switchover; monitor cache hit rates; implement automated routing tests; maintain shard balance; update documentation; perform pre‑switchover checks

original_source: mw-page-content-change-enrich app failure in passive DC due to misconfigured egress rules causing network timeout to thanos-swift
failure_pattern: Misconfigured egress rules prevented the mw-page-content-change-enrich Flink application from establishing a connection to the thanos-swift service in the passive data center, causing a network timeout that stopped the Kubernetes operator from starting the app. The failure was isolated to the passive DC, so there was no impact on the active DC or on end‑user SLOs.
mitigation_principle: implement automated egress rule validation across all DCs; enforce network policy consistency via IaC; add health checks for external dependencies; monitor egress connectivity; document and review egress rules; perform cross‑DC testing before deployment

original_source: Kafka mirror-maker instability when scaling to 15 processes causes replication outage
failure_pattern: Scaling the MirrorMaker from 9 to 15 instances triggered RecordTooLargeException errors on broker 1003, causing the MirrorMaker processes to crash and restart in a loop. The replication between kafka‑main and kafka‑jumbo was blocked for almost 12 hours, leading to delayed updates in the Wikidata Query Service and stale data for users.
mitigation_principle: Limit MirrorMaker instances to a tested stable count; monitor RecordTooLargeException logs; adjust broker max.message.size; isolate configuration changes; perform scaling tests before deployment; upgrade Kafka to a newer stable version; sandbox test instances to prevent production impact

original_source: Flink streaming job failure due to Kafka partition copying causing message processing delays
root_cause_category: resource starvation during Kafka partition reassignment
failure_pattern: During a Kafka partition reassignment, even with throttling, broker threads were starved, causing the Flink enrichment job to fail sending data to Kafka. The resulting backpressure accumulated a backlog of events that persisted until the job’s parallelism was increased, after which the backlog cleared.
mitigation_principle: monitor broker thread utilization during partition reassignment; avoid running single-replica streaming jobs during maintenance; increase parallelism or replicas for streaming jobs; implement backpressure-aware retry logic; coordinate Kafka reassignments with dependent services

original_source: CloudVPS VMs lost network connectivity due to removal of isc-dhcp-client package during package cleanup
failure_pattern: Removal of the isc-dhcp-client package during a package cleanup caused the DHCP client to be missing on bullseye VMs. Without a DHCP client, IP leases expired and the VMs lost network connectivity, bringing down proxies, hosted services, and the monitoring stack. The cascading loss of connectivity resulted in widespread service outages.
mitigation_principle: implement package removal safeguards; add monitoring for critical services; use automated rollback or preflight checks; ensure critical packages are not removed in bulk; add meta-monitoring for metricsinfra; create cookbook for console commands

original_source: ESAMS DC unreachable due to accidental router linecard reboot
root_cause_category: human error causing accidental router linecard reboot
failure_pattern: An accidental reboot of a router linecard in the Amsterdam data center severed network connectivity, causing packet loss and high latency. This dropped request rates from 150k to 91k req/s and made the service unreachable for users, resulting in network errors and delays.
mitigation_principle: Implement strict change management and double‑check procedures; enforce automated safeguards to prevent accidental reboots; provide redundant linecards and automatic failover; monitor linecard health and alert on status changes; require multi‑person approval for critical hardware changes; document and rehearse recovery steps

original_source: Replication failure in etcd-mirror due to event index being cleared after 1,000 non-conftool events
symptoms: conftool changes not replicated between data centers
root_cause_category: etcd event index retention limit exceeded
failure_pattern: A burst of 1,000 non-conftool etcd events exceeded etcd’s 1,000‑event retention window, causing the replication index stored in __replication/conftool to be cleared. The etcd-mirror watcher, which relies on a continuous index, could not recover and stopped replication, leaving conftool data out of sync between the two data centers until the index was manually advanced.
mitigation_principle: implement automatic recovery for cleared event index; switch to etcd v3 or a more resilient replication tool; limit non‑conftool traffic during critical periods; document safe restart procedures for etcd-mirror; monitor event index health and alert on retention breaches

original_source: Elasticsearch Omega Cluster Failure due to Operator Error During Decommissioning
symptoms: search queries failed for omega cluster wikis
failure_pattern: A puppet patch removed omega master nodes during decommissioning, firewalling them off and preventing them from participating in leader election. The cluster lost quorum, causing the search endpoint to return 503 errors and preventing search and indexing for omega cluster wikis.
mitigation_principle: Implement safeguards against mass decommissioning of critical nodes; use staged decommissioning with quorum checks; add automated alerts for cluster state changes; document and review decommissioning procedures; test decommissioning scripts in staging before production

original_source: Outage in eqiad due to increased CoreDNS load from mcrouter daemonset deployment on mw-on-k8s
failure_pattern: The deployment of the mcrouter daemonset changed MediaWiki pods to use an external mcrouter service, which increased DNS queries to CoreDNS from ~40k to ~110k req/s. CoreDNS pods lacked sufficient memory and replicas, leading to OOM kills and crash‑loopbackoff, causing DNS resolution failures that cascaded into higher latency, reduced throughput, and PHP‑FPM worker exhaustion.
mitigation_principle: Ensure resource limits match expected load; perform load testing before deployment; monitor DNS query rates and pod health; use correct FQDN formatting; roll out changes incrementally with automated rollback; implement alerts for OOM events

original_source: Search unavailable for some eqiad users due to missing VLAN configuration on LVS load-balancers after new Elastic hosts were pooled.
failure_pattern: The new Elasticsearch hosts were added to the cluster, but the LVS load balancers lacked the required VLAN sub‑interfaces for the racks they resided in. As a result the load balancer could not reach those hosts, causing connection failures, a spike in downstream errors, incomplete search results, and missing autocomplete for users.
mitigation_principle: implement automated VLAN configuration validation; add health checks for backend connectivity; monitor load balancer backend reachability; enforce configuration drift detection; establish change management for network provisioning

original_source: Toolforge Redis refusing connections due to too many active clients, resolved by restart and failover.
symptoms: tools unable to connect to Redis
root_cause_category: resource exhaustion due to max clients limit
failure_pattern: The Redis instance reached its maximum client limit, causing it to refuse new connections. This resulted in intermittent connection errors for Toolforge tools. Restarting the instance and failing over to a healthy node restored service.
mitigation_principle: implement connection pooling limits; monitor client count and alert before threshold; automate failover and scaling; update runbooks with known issue resolution steps

original_source: Kubernetes API server CPU and network saturation during MediaWiki deployment due to OpenTelemetry collector and infrastructure limitations
failure_pattern: The OpenTelemetry collector was configured with the k8sattributesprocessor, causing a >50% increase in egress traffic from the API servers. This saturated the 1Gbps network links and over‑taxed the API server CPUs, leading to high latency, TCP retransmits, and ultimately failed MediaWiki deployments.
mitigation_principle: Tune OpenTelemetry collector configuration to reduce egress traffic; monitor API server CPU and network usage; use dedicated high‑bandwidth NICs; avoid hardcoding IPs in collector; implement alerting for CPU saturation; perform capacity planning before adding new components

original_source: Image hotlinking caused link saturation in the eqsin datacentre, increasing response times for users.
failure_pattern: Hotlinking of an image on Commons caused a surge of requests to the eqsin datacentre, saturating the outbound port and triggering FastNetMon to detect a DDoS. The saturated link increased latency and produced HTTP 429 responses, leading to degraded user experience.
mitigation_principle: implement rate limiting for hotlinked content; add CDN caching for static assets; monitor port utilization and set alerts; deploy traffic shaping or throttling on saturated links; test hotlinking scenarios in staging; update Varnish rules to block hotlinking; tune FastNetMon thresholds

original_source: Data loss in Labs home directories due to erroneous Puppet symlink
root_cause_category: missing timeout configuration leading to hung rsync processes
failure_pattern: The systemd timer that triggers the rsync client for puppet volatile data had no timeout, allowing the rsync process to hang indefinitely when a deadlock occurred in rsyncd. This prevented the volatile data, including GeoLite2 files, from being synced to puppetmasters, resulting in stale GeoIP data and missing new files for services that rely on them.
mitigation_principle: Add non-infinite TimeoutStartSec to systemd timers; enable monitoring and logging for timer jobs; use rsync --timeout and --contimeout; set up alerts for timer failures; implement end-to-end data freshness checks

original_source: Cloud VPS outage due to faulty optic causing Ceph write stalls
failure_pattern: A faulty optic on the fiber link between WMCS racks caused packet loss, which triggered interface errors on the network switch. The resulting network degradation prevented Ceph from confirming write replication, causing Ceph writes to stall and storage to hang. The stalled storage made Cloud VPS VMs unresponsive, rendering all services hosted on the VPS inaccessible.
mitigation_principle: implement proactive link health monitoring and alerting for interface errors; establish redundant link paths with automatic failover; schedule maintenance with coordinated communication between teams; document and test incident response procedures for network failures; ensure Ceph cluster can tolerate network partitions without stalling writes

original_source: System-wide renaming of Kyverno policies overloaded Toolforge Kubernetes control nodes rendering API unresponsive.
symptoms: unable to create or operate jobs/webservices
root_cause_category: resource limit removal leading to overload
failure_pattern: Removing resource limits for Kyverno and applying a large policy rename caused Kyverno to generate many policy reconciliation events, overloading the Kubernetes API server CPU. The overloaded API server became unresponsive, preventing job and webservice creation and causing kubelet errors and service registration failures.
mitigation_principle: implement strict resource limits for critical controllers; perform load testing before large policy changes; use staged rollout for policy renames; monitor API server CPU and set alerts; deploy registry controller config immediately after rollout

original_source: Wikimedia full dumps caused database pressure and network saturation due to log flooding, resulting in wiki outages.
failure_pattern: The dumps process overloaded the database replicas, causing a surge of errors in MediaWiki. Those errors were emitted via UDP syslog, flooding the network and saturating core routers. The saturated network prevented normal traffic, leading to widespread wiki outages.
mitigation_principle: implement rate limiting on UDP logs; add backpressure or throttling for dump processes; enforce database replica lag thresholds; monitor replica lag; add circuit breakers; use TCP for critical logs; add capacity planning for dumps; add alerting for log volume; use QoS for UDP traffic

original_source: Database overload in s4 and x1 causing wiki unavailability due to excessive write queries
failure_pattern: Excessive write queries (>400 wr/s) overloaded the s4 database servers, triggering circuit breakers that cut off application servers and produced 5XX errors, leading to wiki unavailability. The overload cascaded to x1, amplifying the outage.
mitigation_principle: implement write load monitoring and throttling; set appropriate circuit breaker thresholds; perform capacity planning and scaling; optimize query patterns; schedule maintenance for high‑load queries; enable automated alerts for write rates

original_source: Logstash UI unavailable due to duplicate phatality plugin registration during scap deployment
failure_pattern: The scap deployment script wrapped a plugin‑existence check in an unnecessary sudo, causing the check to fail because the command was not allowlisted. The script then proceeded to install the phatality plugin without removing the old version, resulting in duplicate registration. The opensearch‑dashboards service detected the duplicate plugin as a fatal error, crashed, and the Logstash UI became unavailable.
mitigation_principle: Validate sudoers entries before deployment; add idempotent plugin installation checks; implement pre‑deployment validation to detect duplicate plugin registration; ensure scap deployment halts on early failures; add unit tests for deployment scripts; monitor plugin registration state

original_source: Replication failure in x1 and es6 sections due to pt-heartbeat row mismatch during datacenter switchover preparation
symptoms: no visible errors but potential stale data
failure_pattern: The pt-heartbeat process performs a REPLACE, which in row-based replication is translated to an UPDATE ROW. Because the heartbeat row was missing on the target node, the UPDATE failed, causing the replication channel to stop. The stopped replication left stale data in the affected services while no error was immediately visible to users.
mitigation_principle: Implement post-configuration replication health checks for both directions; use statement-based replication for pt-heartbeat or ensure missing rows are inserted before replication; add monitoring for replication errors and heartbeat table consistency; avoid deleting heartbeat rows without verifying presence on all nodes; document and test replication changes in a staging environment before production deployment

original_source: MariaDB outage due to DIMM error on pc1013 causing service degradation and requiring manual failover to pc1015.
failure_pattern: A DIMM error on host pc1013 caused memory corruption that crashed MariaDB, bringing the host down and disrupting replication. The crash led to packet loss and increased parser activity, degrading wiki read performance until a manual failover to pc1015 was performed and circular replication was re‑established.
mitigation_principle: implement automated hardware health monitoring and failover; automate failover and replication setup; document and automate manual interventions; use redundant memory modules and hot‑swappable hardware; enable proactive memory error detection and alerting

original_source: A core router in eqsin went down due to hardware failure, causing connectivity issues for users in the Asia region.
failure_pattern: A disk failure in the core router caused the device to reboot. During reboot, the router loaded an outdated rescue configuration, preventing it from rejoining the network. This resulted in BGP and OSPF failures, leading to packet loss and connectivity issues for Asia users.
mitigation_principle: automate configuration backup on every commit; enforce no-load backup config; monitor disk health proactively; schedule timely hardware replacement; implement redundant core routers; validate rescue config updates; use configuration management tools

original_source: Parser cache database saturation in codfw due to connection spike and missing query killer, impacting user reads and writes
root_cause_category: connection overload due to missing query killer and scraper activity
failure_pattern: A surge in reparse jobs triggered by a large shared template update caused many parser cache database connections to open. Newly deployed parsercache hosts lacked the query killer, so idle connections were not terminated, leading to saturation of the MariaDB instance. An aggressive scraper further increased parse activity, exacerbating the connection spike and causing the database to become read‑only, which in turn caused page rendering and update failures for users.
mitigation_principle: Implement query killer on all parsercache hosts; enforce connection limits; monitor connection counts; add scraper rate limiting; improve changeprop observability; ensure proper deployment validation; add automated alerts for connection spikes; isolate template updates; use circuit breaker patterns

original_source: WMCS proxy nginx failure due to Puppet removing nameserver IP from configuration files
failure_pattern: A Puppet run removed the nameserver IP from /etc/resolv.conf and from Nginx configuration files, causing DNS resolution failures for Nginx. This led to a fatal error in Nginx, bringing the proxy service down and triggering the ProjectProxyMainProxyDown alert.
mitigation_principle: Ensure idempotent and validated configuration changes; monitor critical config file integrity; add automated tests for puppet modules; create runbooks for proxy downtime; implement alert suppression for known maintenance windows

original_source: WMCS network problems due to OpenStack neutron agent restart causing Toolforge NFS and DNS failures
symptoms: users unable to login to bastions
kubernetes pods crashing due to DNS errors
failure_pattern: A puppet change to the OpenStack OVS configuration triggered a restart of the neutron‑openvswitch‑agent, temporarily severing VM connectivity. The loss of network connectivity caused the Toolforge NFS server to be perceived as down and produced intermittent DNS resolution failures, which in turn led to Kubernetes pod crashes and widespread Toolforge workload failures.
mitigation_principle: implement automated monitoring of network connectivity during agent restarts; add alerting for NFS and DNS service health; enforce pre‑deployment validation of OVS config changes; use rolling restarts with health checks; add network observability and cross‑checks; document and train operators on cluster operations; add DNS monitoring and alerting; prevent puppet from restarting neutron‑openvswitch‑agent automatically

original_source: Port saturation from cached Varnish HEAD-GET upgrades due to Wikimedia Enterprise traffic causing backend cache poisoning.
failure_pattern: Wikimedia Enterprise sent many HEAD requests to ATS. Varnish converted these to GETs and cached the large responses as hit‑for‑pass, poisoning the backend cache and causing ATS to serve large objects repeatedly. The repeated large GETs saturated the inbound port and consumed ATS resources, leading to high port utilization and degraded performance.
mitigation_principle: Add request filtering to skip caching for large HEAD requests; use uncacheable headers or hit‑for‑pass only for specific IPs; block problematic IPs via requestctl; monitor port utilization with specific alerts; coordinate with internal teams before deploying caching changes; test caching logic changes in staging; document incidents and create formal incident docs

original_source: Gerrit largely inaccessible for all users due to incoming traffic impairment
symptoms: Gerrit largely inaccessible for all users
failure_pattern: Incoming traffic impairment caused Gerrit to become largely inaccessible for all users. The traffic issue prevented requests from reaching Gerrit, leading to a widespread outage.
mitigation_principle: Implement traffic monitoring and alerting; add rate limiting and traffic shaping; increase network redundancy; improve incident detection and response procedures

original_source: Outage on maps.wikimedia.org due to misconfigured Kubernetes migration of Kartotherian service
component: Kartotherian Kubernetes deployment (missing LVS loopback IP)
failure_pattern: The Kubernetes nodes were deployed without the required LVS loopback IP, causing traffic sent to the load balancer to loop back and never reach the Kartotherian pods. As a result, the pods never responded, leading ATS to drop connections and overload the remaining bare‑metal nodes, which then produced timeouts and 5xx errors for users.
mitigation_principle: Validate all network configuration settings before pooling traffic; ensure load balancer health checks accurately reflect backend availability; use automated tests for mixed environments; document required settings for new services; monitor traffic dashboards before shifting traffic; perform immediate rollback if new nodes receive zero traffic

original_source: TLS certificate misconfiguration for Kubernetes service caused 31,000 HTTP 50X errors on maps.wikimedia.org
failure_pattern: A missing SAN in the TLS certificate for the Kartotherian service on Kubernetes caused TLS handshakes to fail for requests to maps.wikimedia.org. The failed handshakes resulted in HTTP 5xx responses, leading to widespread service unavailability for users.
mitigation_principle: automated TLS certificate validation before deployment; enforce SAN inclusion for all domain-facing services; monitor TLS handshake failures and 5xx error rates as part of SLOs; document and audit certificate configurations; perform sanity checks during deployment

original_source: Wikidata Query Service experiences increased 500 errors following MediaWiki extension deployment.
failure_pattern: A MediaWiki extension deployment introduced changes that caused the Wikidata Query Service to return 500 errors for user queries. The failure manifested as a rapid rise in error rates, triggering alerts and prompting a rollback of the extension, after which the error rate returned to normal.
mitigation_principle: Review and document service dependencies before deployment; implement automated integration tests covering external service contracts; enforce strict contract compliance; monitor error rates and set alerts for abnormal spikes; use feature flags or staged rollouts; establish rapid rollback procedures

original_source: Infinite redirect of www.wikipedia.org due to incorrect Apache configuration deployment
failure_pattern: A deployment of an incorrect Apache configuration caused www.wikipedia.org to redirect to itself, creating an infinite 301 loop. Cached responses delayed detection, leading to a slow ramp‑up of outages as caches expired. Users experienced "Too Many Redirects" errors and could not access the homepage.
mitigation_principle: implement automated redirect loop detection tests; enforce strict configuration validation before deployment; use staged rollouts with immediate cache purging; monitor redirect status codes with higher sensitivity; maintain clear incident tagging for critical entry points

original_source: Flink taskmanager OOM caused pipeline failure and Kafka consumer lag in mw-content-history-reconcile-enrich job
failure_pattern: The monthly reconcile DAG produced a large spike in events (6.3M vs 11K), causing the Flink TaskManager to consume more memory than allocated, leading to an out‑of‑memory error and repeated restarts that hit the restart limit, which in turn caused the pipeline to fail and Kafka consumer lag until the memory was increased.
mitigation_principle: Implement dynamic scaling based on event volume; set memory limits and monitor OOM events; add alerting for high throughput spikes; retain historical metrics for trend analysis; enforce resource quotas to prevent OOM

original_source: Upload cache unavailability due to Swift overload from excessive .tiff file downloads
failure_pattern: Excessive downloads of .tiff files overloaded the Swift frontend in eqiad, causing 5xx errors that propagated to ATS, HAProxy, and Varnish, which in turn reported reduced HTTP availability and led to high latency and error messages for users accessing upload.wikimedia.org.
mitigation_principle: Implement traffic throttling and rate limiting for high-volume downloads; add load monitoring and auto-scaling for Swift; enforce request quotas and user-agent filtering; improve alerting thresholds and visibility; add redundancy and failover for Swift storage

original_source: Sessionstore unavailability due to Cassandra disk exhaustion from high session write rates
failure_pattern: Rapid growth of session write operations filled the storage devices of the Cassandra nodes, causing disk exhaustion. The exhausted disks led to node failures and loss of quorum, which in turn made the sessionstore service unavailable and caused edit failures for users.
mitigation_principle: Implement proactive disk utilization alerts; add capacity planning and monitoring for write growth; tune compaction and garbage collection; partition namespace to limit growth; establish automated truncation or graceful degradation policies; enable alerts for node failures

original_source: Gerrit data corruption due to split-brain replication during host switchover
symptoms: missing or unmerged changes in Gerrit UI
root_cause_category: split-brain replication due to DNS change during switchover
failure_pattern: During the DNS switchover both Gerrit hosts were treated as primary, causing concurrent replication. The older host replicated an outdated state to the new primary, overwriting newer changes and corrupting repositories, which manifested as missing or unmerged changes in the UI.
mitigation_principle: Ensure only one primary during switchover; disable replication on replicas during host changes; take snapshots before switchover; enable backups on all hosts; verify replication status via monitoring; enforce role::gerrit defaults to replica; remove unnecessary SSH access; assert DNS resolution consistency; split Puppet roles into primary/replica; add local backup step to switchover cookbook

original_source: Footnote rendering broken in mobile apps due to removal of transitional CSS rule during Parsoid Cite migration
symptoms: footnotes rendered as [0] instead of correct numbers
failure_pattern: The removal of a transitional CSS rule that suppressed old footnote localization caused the mobileapps PCS to serve outdated CSS alongside new HTML footnote markers, leading to rendering of all footnotes as [0] and making them unclickable.
mitigation_principle: automated style synchronization between services; automated integration tests for rendering; alerting on test failures; change management for breaking changes; document and communicate breaking changes; use feature flags for CSS changes

original_source: Cloud VPS security groups deleted due to buggy IPv6 migration script causing service outages
symptoms: network timeouts due to blocked ports
failure_pattern: A script intended to migrate security group rules to IPv6 contained a bug that caused existing rules to be deleted instead of updated. The removal of these rules blocked critical network ports, leading to network timeouts and the outage of services such as Quarry, Toolforge, and Prometheus.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated validation and dry‑run for security group updates; enforce strict quota checks and error handling in scripts; maintain recent backups and quick restore procedures; separate test and production environments for migration scripts; monitor security group rule changes and alert on anomalies

original_source: Traffic surge from papal announcement causes brief European outages despite record-breaking load
failure_pattern: The sudden traffic surge from the papal announcement pushed the legacy IPVS load balancer in the esams datacenter beyond its packet and connection handling limits, causing probe failures, elevated network error logs, and full queues. These failures cascaded to the application layer, resulting in error pages and slow responses for European users.
mitigation_principle: Deploy scalable load balancer (Liberica/Katran) to handle high packet rates; monitor load balancer metrics and set alerts for packet/connection thresholds; implement auto‑scaling and traffic rebalancing across datacenters; use request coalescing and multi‑DC read replicas; perform ongoing performance cleanup to reduce lock contention

original_source: Missing autocomplete indices due to failed daily job and OpenSearch migration patch
symptoms: search bar not returning expected results
failure_pattern: The daily job that creates autocomplete indices failed on 2025‑05‑07, leaving a subset of English Wikipedia articles missing from the autocomplete index. A subsequent OpenSearch migration patch was merged, which cancelled the next day’s job and prevented the missing indices from being rebuilt. Consequently, users typing in the Wikipedia search bar received incomplete or stale autocomplete suggestions.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated job health checks and alerts; enforce pre‑merge testing for job‑impacting patches; maintain manual job trigger or fallback; separate critical jobs from patch deployments; add redundancy or backup indices; monitor job status and auto‑retry; document and review job dependencies

original_source: OpenSearch clusters unavailable due to removal of hosts with primary shards during decommissioning
failure_pattern: During a planned decommission, hosts were banned without checking for primary shard ownership. The removal of nodes that still held primary shards caused 60 indices to enter a red (unwriteable) state, which in turn broke the update pipeline and triggered alerts. The cluster was restored by deleting the red indices and rebalancing shards.
mitigation_principle: Plan decommissioning with shard allocation awareness; test node removal in staging; maintain up-to-date snapshots and recovery procedures; avoid suppressing alerts during maintenance; document and automate runbooks for large-scale node removal; create ops-focused dashboards for monitoring cluster health

original_source: Data loss in eventgate-analytics due to inadvertent MediaWiki config change disabling EventBus logging
symptoms: missing data in downstream Hive and Kafka tables
failure_pattern: An inadvertent change to the MediaWiki configuration disabled EventBus logging, which caused event production to drop gradually as the queue drained. This prevented eventgate-analytics from emitting events, leading to missing data in downstream Hive and Kafka consumers and resulting in data loss for several streams.
mitigation_principle: implement automated alerts for drastic changes in event production rates; enforce configuration change reviews and automated tests for logging settings; add monitoring of EventBus logs; use configuration management to detect unintended changes; maintain SLOs that monitor traffic drops

original_source: Cirrussearch outage due to split-brain during rolling restart of master-eligible node in EQIAD cluster
failure_pattern: A rolling restart of the master‑eligible node cirrussearch1100 caused it to come up with stale cluster state, creating a split‑brain and loss of quorum. The cluster could not elect a leader, so all API calls failed. After the node was depooled, stopped, and its data directory removed, the cluster regained quorum and recovered.
mitigation_principle: follow master‑eligible replacement procedure; depool node before restart; validate cluster state before bringing node back; document recovery steps; add alerts for 503/no cluster leader; test rolling restarts in staging; enforce pre‑restart checks; maintain quorum during maintenance

original_source: Ceph issues due to Bookworm upgrade caused intermittent failures in Toolforge and Cloud VPS
symptoms: HTTP requests to Toolforge tools fail
High number of slow Ceph operations
failure_pattern: The upgrade of six Ceph hosts to Debian Bookworm introduced incompatibilities with the Ceph Pacific software, causing a surge in slow operations and OSD failures. The degraded Ceph performance led to timeouts and unresponsive services in Toolforge and Cloud VPS, resulting in intermittent downtime. The problem persisted until the affected hosts were re‑imaged back to Bullseye, restoring Ceph stability.
mitigation_principle: perform thorough compatibility testing before OS upgrades; implement automated health checks and alerting for Ceph slow ops; use staged rollouts with rollback capability; ensure sufficient monitoring and paging for critical services; maintain documentation of upgrade procedures

original_source: Cite + VisualEditor list-defined reference disappearances due to flawed Cite extension deployment
symptoms: Cite errors appear as red text
failure_pattern: A patch to the Cite extension removed the ID attribute from list-defined reference <li> elements during serialization. Parsoid, which relies on that ID to detect existing references, interpreted the missing IDs as deletions, causing all list-defined references to be dropped when a page was saved. Consequently, any page edited with Visual Editor lost its list-defined references, resulting in missing citations and red error text.
mitigation_principle: implement automated tests for Visual Editor to Parsoid conversion; use feature flags for extension deployments; require code review and regression testing for serialization changes; monitor for missing IDs in <references> tags

original_source: Cirrussearch outage due to split-brain during rolling restart of master-eligible node in EQIAD cluster
failure_pattern: A rolling restart of the master‑eligible node cirrussearch1100 was performed without following the documented replacement procedure, causing the node to come up with stale master data. This created a split‑brain situation, the cluster lost quorum, and all API calls failed, resulting in user‑facing search failures.
mitigation_principle: Follow documented master‑eligible replacement procedure; depool master‑eligible nodes before restart; use rolling restart scripts that handle master‑eligible nodes safely; add pre‑restart quorum checks; document and automate recovery steps; implement alerts that include specific error codes; test restart procedures in staging; enforce change‑management approvals

original_source: WDQS service outage due to simultaneous Blazegraph deadlock in codfw hosts
failure_pattern: A deadlock in Blazegraph on one node triggered a cascading deadlock that spread to all codfw hosts, causing the entire WDQS cluster to become unresponsive. The load balancer detected no healthy nodes and routed traffic to a pool with no available servers, resulting in 500 errors for all queries.
mitigation_principle: implement automated deadlock detection and recovery; add per-node health checks that detect deadlock state; increase node isolation to prevent cascading failures; add circuit breaker to isolate failing nodes; improve monitoring of deadlock metrics; enable automatic restarts or failover for deadlocked nodes; add redundancy and load balancer health checks to avoid routing to deadlocked nodes
